content.text:
Let's start our process of rolling out just print V2 in small batches, come up with a plan so that we will have the correct correct rollout sequence to make sure that dependencies are in place at every step of the rollout, as well as to make sure we start from smaller, more enthusiastic group and slowly expand that to large audience, mostly the current obigo and just print v1 current user base.

Draft a high-level plan for me, and I will provide my feedback.

items.content: Gather what the release depends on
Check release mechanics and user groups
Draft the rollout plan

- Alias "slicer-1" / "Slicer 1"; efforts "fast"/"thorough" map to low/high at the gateway. First upstream claude-sonnet-5-5.

GET /v2/models gives each alias's "format" for this person (server-side A/B by hash of user id). Each chat is pinned to the format of its first request (ChatModelChoice.format in the project doc); new chats take the current assignment.
- New OAuth app client_id "JusPrin2" (public, authorization code, PKCE, redirect http://127.0.0.1/callback with no port; DOT 2.3 accepts any loopback port). Created by hand in admin like v1's "JusPrin" (README_jusprin_server.md), no migration.
- v1 import on first launch: copy user/ + BambuNetworkEngine.conf + JusPrin.conf→JusPrin2.conf, v1 access_token becomes jusprin_agent/jusprin_api_key; welcome-back window from canvas boards V1-01..03. Kenneth will not rotate the dotenv.example key.

Where: client worktree `.claude/worktrees/jusprin-cloud-provider` (branch claude/jusprin-cloud-provider on d921c4b3dd, Release build dir); server worktree `~/Projects/tsd-enterprise-worktrees/jusprin-cloud` (claude/jusprin-cloud-gateway) with obico-server on claude/jusprin-v2-oauth-app. Pushed 2026-10-24 as one commit each: client branch `claude/jusprin-cloud-provider` (`ac55c2961a`, TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin), tsd-enterprise `claude/jusprin-cloud-gateway` (`3b54e5928f`, kennethjiang/tsd-enterprise; includes the large-request slots, shared upstream client, off-loop parse). obico-server has NO changes: Kenneth hasn't decided whether v2 is open-sourced, so the README commit was dropped and the compose change skipped. ops branch `claude/jusprin-v2-gateway-routing` handled by the ASGI side session. Staging is live at https://app-stg.obico.io; prod NOT rolled out.

**Production rollout 2026-10-25 (Kenneth asked, without deciding the domain):** gateway 3b54e5928f merged to tsd-enterprise master; release branch df39c0dcfd (bundles copied from the previous release 76d9f2d602 because frontend/obico-server were unchanged) → CircleCI built `kennethjiang/web_ent:obi.4048`; staging and prod run it; prod Secret/ConfigMap `jusprin-v2-gateway-prod` (keys copied from the stg Secret), JusPrin2 OAuth app id 9 on prod (owner user 1), ingress rules on app.obico.io / app.thespaghettidetective.com / app.kingroon.com (kingroon's cert expired 2025-05-15, pre-existing). ops master 272cde9. Client merged to jusprin-newui as 889d28681c (pushed). No-model smoke script pattern: short-lived AccessToken for the JusPrin2 app owner, `unknown_model` bodies per format (the gateway rejects foreign fields first), delete the token. GCE was out of capacity for node scale-up in us-central1-c during the rollout; it still fit. Probing the stream paths before the URL map propagates (~2.5 min) creates a Sentry ImproperlyConfigured issue (1963, resolved).

**Still open (Kenneth, 2026-10-24): whether JusPrin gets a dedicated domain instead of app.obico.io** — now: decide before the JusPrin 2 desktop app ships with that default. It moves the client's default gateway (ProviderProfile.hpp "jusprin" row), the OAuth sign-in pages and login cookies, the prod ingress rules and certificate, and imported v1 base_url values. Reminders sit in ProviderProfile.hpp, web_ent/jusprin/v2/urls.py and the ops RUNBOOK/prod draft.

Local server: compose project `jusprin-cloud` on port 3434 (Kenneth's own stack holds 3334), fake upstream `web_ent/scripts/jusprin/fake_upstream.py --port 8765`; test account in LOCAL_TEST_ACCOUNT.txt. The session cookie is scoped to ".localhost", so a Python cookie jar won't send it back to localhost: pass it as a header.

**Prod topology finding:** tsdweb-prod is gunicorn sync workers; only tsdws-prod runs daphne (`config.asgi:application`). The gateway's two streaming paths are a raw ASGI endpoint (Django 4.0 can't stream async) behind a router set as ASGI_APPLICATION, so prod needs an ingress rule sending them to tsdws-prod. Kenneth wants a simple single-Django-project topology; decision pending. Compose files that start daphne with `config.routing:application` bypass the router.

**End-to-end run, 2026-10-24 (all passed after one fix):** v1 import → welcome window (V1-02 with real data, V1-03 with a revoked token) → chat through /v2/responses → server switched to anthropic → old chat stayed on /responses, new chat went to /messages → in-app browser sign-in via OrcaSlicer's loopback 41172 → sign-out revoked the token (200 → 401). The run found that /jusprin/api/me/ nests the email under "user" (fixed). Tooling in `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/cloud-e2e/` (instrumented page server, browser stand-in that logs in with the test account, fake v1 builder, run.sh).

Traps from that run: hook `window.__jusprinBridge` with a defineProperty setter, or a polling hook misses the handshake and the window looks silent; serve the instrumented page with Cache-Control: no-store (WKWebView reuses the previous run's page); a v1 settings file (version 1.4.0) makes Orca show its modal "Profile syncing change" notice at start-up, which posted keys can't dismiss but an AppleScript click on its AXCloseButton can; a fixture v1 settings file needs the `models` list or no system profiles load and every imported preset looks orphaned.

Kenneth, 2026-11-07, reviewing the first-launch flow page (https://claude.ai/artifact/LV1mW9VHJvP4skpSyEbcEs):
- "JusPrin v1 account will not be shared with v2. So there is no such thing as signing with V1 account." "the only place where V2 and V1 overlap is V2 will import V1 printers/profiles etc. in a way that's very similar to importing from orcaslicer."
- "the screens for three different ways of setting up printers/profiles etc, import from v1, import from orcasslicer, and manual, should have the links for the user to switch to other methods. Basically all these three methods should be discoverable no matter if anything, or what is found."

As of ui-walkthrough 2599bc350c the code contradicts this: V1Import copies silently at start-up, WelcomeBackWindow checks the v1 sign-in and makes its own sign-up offer over the welcome, OnboardingModel skips the Printers step after a v1 import, and the welcome's sign-up card shows a v1 kept-price line.

Agreed by Kenneth the same day ("Yes, all three", flow page version 3): the JusPrin 1 screen opens first when both are found; a link to an app that wasn't found asks for its folder, then shows that import screen; File › Import gains Import from JusPrin 1… next to Import from OrcaSlicer…. Canvas v149 drew all of this (boards first-run-19, 20; Other ways on 07, 08, 18; File › Import item; 1c/1d superseded).

**Why:** Kenneth found the first launch confusing in testing; v1 account handling and a missing import path were agent inventions.

**How to apply:** never design or build a v1 sign-in, account check or v1-specific welcome. Treat v1 like OrcaSlicer: asked, ticked list, Import, result screen. Every printer setup screen carries links to the other two ways. Related: [[v1-import-scope-origin]], [[first-run-flow-sequence]].

Built (uncommitted when written): a "Get the new version…" button that does what Help › Check for Updates does (`check_for_updates()` in ShellController.cpp: check now, then Preferences › Updates). It sits on a chat reply refused with update_required, as the JusPrin row of the model picker, in place of Send report on Home's report form, and in the "Couldn't open project" dialog for a project a newer JusPrin saved (`show_open_failure`). Every button calls `get_new_version()`, which first clears `jusprin_update_skipped` (`UpdateCheck::unskip`): without it, a person who had clicked "Skip this version" was sent to an Updates page saying "Up to date" (reproduced with a test feed on port 18767, then fixed). Same day, second pass (canvas version 175): the button also sits under a sign-in the server refused (shared SignInDoor `outdated` + `SignInActions.getNewVersion`; Home sends `check_for_updates`, its snapshot carries `signInOutdated`) and in Preferences › Account when signed in and the model list is refused (`AccountRow outdatedMessage`, in place of Try again); inside Preferences the page turns to Updates itself. Get the new version to keep using your account." The picker names a JusPrin alias as "JusPrin" (also in New chats start with) and shows no tick when the list is refused. The server minimum must only be raised to a release already on GitHub, or Updates says "Up to date".

=== allauth-65-upgrade.md
---
name: allauth-65-upgrade
description: "2026-11-03 django-allauth 0.63.6 → 65.21.1 upgrade in tsd-enterprise: done in the obico-server submodule's working tree, uncommitted (Kenneth commits submodules); where the patches and breaking-change list are; what the in-app sign-in rebuild must do next."
metadata:
  type: project
---

Kenneth had allauth upgraded first, as its own task, so the in-app email sign-in (`web_ent/jusprin/v2/sign_in.py`, branch `claude/email-sign-in`) can later be rebuilt on allauth's own flows (login by code, email-only sign-up by code, headless with a django-oauth-toolkit token hook). Session: Opus 5.5, worktree `~/Projects/tsd-enterprise-worktrees/email-sign-in`.

**State on 2026-11-03 evening:** allauth 65.21.1 in `obico-server/backend` (Pipfile, Pipfile.lock, requirements.txt), uncommitted in the submodule, nothing on `claude/email-sign-in` changed. Changes: `ACCOUNT_LOGIN_METHODS = {'username'}` + `ACCOUNT_SIGNUP_FIELDS = ['email*','password1*','password2*']` (what allauth derives from the old settings), `account.W001` silenced with a comment, `SyndicateSpecificAccountAdapter.get_client_ip` reads X-Forwarded-For via django-ipware (allauth 65.14.2 stopped trusting it, so everyone behind the load balancer would share one rate limit), allauth's test helpers copied into `site_specific_allauth_google_provider/allauth_testing.py`. Lock also moved Django 5.2.19, oauthlib 4.0.1, sqlparse 0.6.1. Patches and the breaking-change table: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_4d17825a-ac19-4732-a080-7e0c1dca6d1c/` (`allauth-65-1-upgrade.patch`, `allauth-65-2-client-ip.patch`, `allauth-0.63.6-to-65.21.1-changes.md`).

**Verified:** web_ent 180 tests OK, obico-server 119 OK (2 new), the 22 in-app sign-in tests OK; website compared old vs new on two brands with a script, 66 of 82 steps identical, the rest: social error page 401 not 200, `?next=` to another site now goes to `/` (was an open redirect), reset message gained a period, attribute order. Not verified: Google/Apple sign-in to completion (no credentials), client IP behind the real load balancer.

**How to apply:** before turning on `ACCOUNT_EMAIL_VERIFICATION_BY_CODE_ENABLED`, change `send_confirmation_mail` in the account adapter (allauth 65 passes a verification-process object, not an EmailConfirmation). input.recap: Drafted a five-step rollout for JusPrin 2, from the team to the whole Obico user base, with what must be live on the server before each step. Nothing was changed; the plan waits for your feedback.

content.text:
Here is a draft plan for rolling out JusPrin 2 in five steps. It starts with the team, then hand-picked testers, then a public beta. After that it goes to all JusPrin 1 users, and last to the much larger Obico user base. Each step lists what has to be live before it starts, and what we watch before moving to the next one.

## Two facts that shape the plan

- **The app already supports a beta track.** If we publish a build as a GitHub prerelease (for example `2.0.0-beta.1`), only people already running a beta build are told about it. Someone running a normal release never sees it ([ReleaseFeed.cpp:23](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/ReleaseFeed.cpp:23)). So during the early steps, a tester has to be sent the download link. Anyone who finds the link can still install it, so this keeps the group small but doesn't lock it.
- **I don't think publishing 2.0.0 will reach JusPrin 1 users by itself.** This is my hypothesis, not checked against the released 1.4.0. The JusPrin 1 branch looks for updates at OrcaSlicer's own update server, not at our GitHub releases. If that's right, we reach JusPrin 1 and Obico users only by email or by notices we control. The upside is that we decide how fast each group hears about it.

## What must be live before anyone outside the team installs it

1. **The production server.** Today `jusprinv2.obico.io` doesn't resolve, and the staging host `jusprinv2-stg.obico.io` does. Production needs the same setup staging has: the DNS name, ingress and certificate, the JusPrin 2 brand in the production database, the JusPrin 2 sign-in client, and Google sign-in pointed at the new host. It also needs the server code staging runs (email-code sign-in, the credit ledger, the account page data, the oldest-allowed-app-version check). Production was still on build obi.4055 as of my last notes.
2. **Credits that work.** Every new account gets its 500 starting credits, and the model spend per chat matches the $0.30–0.56 we measured.
3. **Signed builds** for all three systems, from the release workflow.
4. **A way to cut off a bad build.** The server setting `JUSPRIN_V2_MIN_APP_VERSION` makes an app older than a given version stop using the account and show "Get the new version…". It only works if a fixed build is already published.
5. **Support.** The `jusprin-support@obico.io` mailbox and Help › Report a problem both reach someone.

## The steps

**1. Team only (a few days).** We install from a prerelease on Mac, Windows and Linux. We sign up with real accounts against production, import from JusPrin 1 and from OrcaSlicer, chat, slice and print. We move on when nobody hits a crash or a failed sign-in.

**2. Hand-picked testers (about 20–50 people).** These are active JusPrin 1 users, people who file good issues, and people who bring their own API key. Payments can stay off at this step, so testers only use their starting credits. We tell them up front that on Mac and Windows, JusPrin 2 replaces JusPrin 1. Going back means reinstalling 1.4, and their JusPrin 1 folder is never touched. We watch crash reports in Sentry, sign-up completion, credit spend per chat, and what they say.

**3. Public beta (a few hundred people).** We announce an opt-in beta to the JusPrin community. Before this step the v2 pricing page and checkout must be live, because `/ent/jusprin/pricing/` is still the v1 page. That way we see real buying behavior. We fix what the testers found and ship new beta builds, which update themselves for beta users.

**4. All JusPrin 1 users.** We publish `2.0.0` as a normal release and move `main` forward to it. Before we email anyone, you move JusPrin 1 subscribers onto their kept price by hand, as you decided. Then we email JusPrin 1 users in waves of about 10%, 30% and then the rest, a few days apart, and watch support volume between waves.

**5. Obico users.** These are the largest group, and their Obico account is separate from a new JusPrin account. We email them in waves too, and could add a notice in the Obico app and website. Before this step, someone should check the Obico Premium discount ($8/$16) end to end. The server finds it by looking for a paying Obico account with the same email. Someone who signs up for JusPrin with a different email gets no discount.

## Decisions for you

**Decision needed: should the early steps be limited by invitation on the server, or is a private download link enough?** A private link costs nothing to set up. The risk is that the link gets passed around, and every stranger who signs up gets 500 free credits that cost us real model spend. A server-side invite list caps that, but someone has to build and test it before step 2. I haven't checked whether the server already has anything like it. I'd go with the private link and watch daily sign-ups, adding the invite list only if they jump. Do you agree?

**Decision needed: should payments be on from step 2, or only from step 3?** Turning them on at step 2 tests checkout with friendly users but holds step 2 until the v2 pricing page is built. Waiting until step 3 lets testing start as soon as the server is live. I'd wait until step 3. Do you agree?

If you'd like this as a page to share with the team, I can publish it.

input.ask: Should I start the production server push?

content.text:
Yes, the next step is the production server, and less of it is missing than my plan said. Payments are built, and production already runs them. What's left is putting the JusPrin 2 host (`jusprinv2.obico.io`) live there, plus a few small server changes staging already has.

## Your three comments

**Payments.** You're right, and my notes were out of date. Your commit `f880ea5076` from 2026-11-07 added the plans and prices page, the billing page and Chargebee checkout. Production has run it since server build obi.4088. So the question of when to turn payments on goes away. One thing I couldn't check: the commit says checkout can't complete until Chargebee's live site has these four entries:
- `jusprin-hobby-monthly`
- `jusprin-workshop-monthly`
- the `jusprin-credit-pack` addon
- the `jusprin2-obico-premium-20` coupon

**Beta track.** You haven't missed anything; it isn't needed. A beta track only helps when some people get updates and others shouldn't, and right now nobody runs a published JusPrin 2. Since JusPrin 1 doesn't tell its users about our GitHub releases, who hears about 2.0.0 depends only on who we contact. So we publish 2.0.0 as a normal release and control the size of each group with outreach. Bug fixes then go out as 2.0.1 and later, and the app tells everyone already running JusPrin 2. I'm dropping the beta track from the plan.

**Reaching people.** Agreed. Each step after the team-only step is an email or message we send by hand, in waves.

## What the production push involves

Production runs build obi.4088 and staging runs obi.4096. These are the changes production would gain:
- **Oldest-version cutoff.** The server can tell an app that's too old to update.
- **Sign-in fix.** Signing in works for someone whose email already has a verified Obico account.
- **Host decides the brand.** The brand now comes from the host, and the website's own login and sign-up are hidden on JusPrin 2's host. This is the only change that touches the Obico website. It went to staging today, so I'd check login on `app-stg.obico.io` before releasing.
- **Terms and Privacy links.** They now go to JusPrin's own pages. This one is on master but not built into any release yet.

Then come the host steps from the ops runbook:
1. **DNS.** Add an A record for `jusprinv2` at Namecheap, pointing to the same static IP as `app.obico.io`. The name doesn't resolve today. You'd have to do this one, since it needs your Namecheap sign-in.
2. **Certificate and routing.** Add a production certificate and a `jusprinv2.obico.io` rule to the ingress, then apply both. The ingress is shared with `app.obico.io`, so I'd diff it against what's live before applying.
3. **Brand setup.** On a production web pod, reset the brand table's id counter and run `set_up_jusprinv2_syndicate jusprinv2.obico.io --google-from app.obico.io`.
4. **Google sign-in.** Add `https://jusprinv2.obico.io/accounts/google/login/callback/` as a redirect address in the Google Cloud console.
5. **Smoke test.** Sign up with an email code and with Google, run a chat, and open the prices page. A real purchase on the live site would be yours to make.

The JusPrin 2 sign-in client and the model gateway's keys are already in production from the October rollout.

Before the JusPrin 2 server goes live in production, find out whether JusPrin 2's Chargebee setup and payment flow are ready, and test them end to end on staging. Report what works, what's missing, and what has to be created or changed on Chargebee's live site before the production push. Don't change anything in production, and don't change Chargebee's live site without Kenneth's explicit yes.

What to check:
1. **Chargebee configuration, test site and live site.** Server commit `f880ea5076` in `~/Projects/tsd-enterprise` (`web_ent/jusprin/ledger/billing.py`, `web_ent/jusprin/jusprin_cb_views.py`, `web_ent/app_ent/cb_views.py`) says checkout can't complete until these exist: item prices `jusprin-hobby-monthly` and `jusprin-workshop-monthly`, the addon `jusprin-credit-pack`, and the coupon `jusprin2-obico-premium-20`. Check each on the test site and the live site with read-only API calls. Also list any other Chargebee setup the code depends on: webhook endpoints and their events, the customer id format `jusprinv2-<user id>`, the hosted page settings, the portal, the currency, and any yearly price ids the code references. 2. **Chargebee emails.** Find out which emails Chargebee sends for JusPrin 2 purchases: receipts, invoices, subscription confirmation, renewal, cancellation, failed payment. Check the sender name and address, the branding, and the wording, including whether they say Obico or JusPrin. Check this on both sites. Say which emails are on and what each one looks like.
3. **Payment flow on staging, end to end.** Use `jusprinv2-stg.obico.io` with the Chargebee test site and its published test cards. Cover buying the credit pack, subscribing to Hobby, changing to Workshop, cancelling, the Obico Premium discount for an email that has a paying Obico account, and a failed card. After each one, check that the right credits were granted exactly once (`CreditGrant` with `source_ref`), that the done page says the right thing, and that the billing page and the app's Preferences › Account show it. Do it from the JusPrin 2 desktop app where you can: the app opens these pages through `/v2/web_link`. For the steps that need a browser, a browser alone is fine. Also check the signed-out prices page (`?guest=1`).
4. **Other settings production needs before launch**, besides Chargebee. content.text:
All three sessions have reported back, and nothing in production or Chargebee has changed. Production can't take JusPrin 2 payments yet: Chargebee's live site has none of JusPrin 2's plans, the credit pack or the Obico discount coupon. The server push is ready, and it's waiting on you for two steps only you can do and a go-ahead. One more gap turned up: production's model-gateway settings are in an old format, and the server rejects them. So chat would fail even once the host is live. I've passed that to the push session, which will ask you before changing them.

## Things only you can do now

Both are safe to do before the host goes live:
1. **DNS.** In Namecheap, open obico.io, then Advanced DNS, and add an A record with host `jusprinv2` and value `34.95.90.112`.
2. **Google sign-in.** On [Obico's Google sign-in client](https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/clients/268097575721-ubm4silcbif4sgsc6qpfuc91403s04o2.apps.googleusercontent.com?project=gettsdapp-843e9), add `https://jusprinv2.obico.io/accounts/google/login/callback/` as an authorized redirect URI.

Payments also need someone to type Chargebee's test card numbers into staging checkout, including a declined card. The Chargebee session wasn't allowed to enter cards, so the card checkout and Chargebee's emails are still untested.

## Decisions needed

**Decision needed: release the new server build with a short window of errors for logged-out visitors?** The build includes a database change that removes a table the current production code reads on the login, sign-up and password-reset pages. The push session expects, from reading the code, that logged-out visitors on not-yet-replaced pods get server errors for about 10–15 minutes. That traffic is light: about three page loads in 30 minutes. The other option is to split the change across two releases, which costs another staging round. I'd accept the window. Go ahead?

**Decision needed: should JusPrin 2 buyers see Obico's branding in checkout and emails?** Chargebee has one logo and one set of email templates per site. Today a JusPrin 2 buyer gets "Obico Admin" emails saying "Thank you for supporting Obico!" There are three options:
- Ship as is. It costs nothing but will confuse buyers.
- Add JusPrin wording to each email template for the JusPrin plans. That's an hour or two of editing in Chargebee, and the checkout logo stays Obico's.
- Make a separate Chargebee site for JusPrin. That gives full branding, but needs new keys, a new webhook and a code change.

I'd add the JusPrin wording to the templates before the email waves. Which do you want?

**Decision needed: fix three billing bugs found on staging?**
- Hobby credits are granted before the first invoice is paid, so a failed renewal still gives a month of credits.
- Moving from Workshop back to Hobby in the same month keeps Workshop's 2,000 credits.
- After a cancel, Preferences › Account still says "Renews 10 Dec."

There's a proposed patch for the first two. The third needs a new server field and an app change. I'd fix all three before payments go live. Should I?

**Decision needed: how do yearly JusPrin 1 subscribers keep their price?** There are 20 paying JusPrin 1 subscribers: 5 monthly at $6.99 and 15 yearly at $59.99. Hobby has no yearly plan, so the proposal bills yearly subscribers $5.00 a month instead. Adding a yearly Hobby plan would take about a day of server work. Either way, each move is done by hand in Chargebee: move the subscription to the new JusPrin 2 account, then set its price. That needs Chargebee Support to switch on the move feature. One known gap: the app would show "$10 a month" to someone paying $6.99. I'd go with $5.00 a month. Agree?

**Decision needed: keep renewing JusPrin 1 subscriptions for people who never move?** I'd say yes, until you set a date to shut JusPrin 1 down. Agree?

**Decision needed: should JusPrin 2's Obico discount continue after the person's Obico subscription ends?** Today the 20% off is a coupon added once at checkout, and it lasts forever. Keeping it in step with the Obico subscription would take about a day to build. I'd leave it checkout-only. Agree?

## Other findings

- 332 accounts used JusPrin 1 in the last 30 days, and 768 in the last 90. About 3,100 Obico accounts qualify for the discount.
- Someone who signs up for JusPrin 2 with a different email gets no Obico discount, and nothing tells them why.
- A possible bug, from reading the code only: when one email has both an Obico and a JusPrin 2 account, a new Obico subscription might not be recorded.

Production and staging both run the same server build, obi.4104, so a new production release would carry only what's on tsd-enterprise master since then. That's five commits:
- **Two code commits from the [JusPrin 1 users session](#local_87a60f59-f953-4ea7-b0fb-1f96b66823b6).** `43840b75e3` adds the yearly Hobby and Workshop plans. It includes a database migration, `0004_plan_billed_price`. `a6745635ed` adds the warning that a moved JusPrin 1 customer loses their old price if they switch plans.
- **Three doc-only commits** about setting up the JusPrin host.

The newest obico-server change, password-reset pages with each brand's logo, is already in obi.4104.

I've asked four sessions:
- **[JusPrin 1 users](#local_87a60f59-f953-4ea7-b0fb-1f96b66823b6):** should the yearly plans ship now, and what must be ready first?
- **[Chargebee check](#local_1ae65d86-2760-4594-94a2-157beb64e86e):** does the live Chargebee site have the yearly prices, and does it have unreleased server work?
- **[Production push](#local_2e8b84da-58b4-4ef1-bd87-b76f805fdf4d):** do it or the sessions it started have anything waiting on a release?
- **[PayPal checkout fix](#local_92607d89-53ce-49de-b66c-6c7f1e5b7f3f):** does its fix need the server at all?

None of them will release anything. Two of them were mid-turn, so their answers may take a while. I'll put the answers together for you as they come in.

Releasing the yearly-plan commits (43840b75e3, a6745635ed): no code or settings change is needed, but run them on staging first. They have only been tested locally.

1. Ship now or wait. They can ship now. Nothing else of mine in tsd-enterprise is uncommitted. One related branch is committed but not on master: jusprin1-pending-moves (60ead684fc). It is a read-only management command that lists JusPrin 1 subscribers who now also have a JusPrin 2 account. Kenneth needs it before moving anyone, but it doesn't have to be in this release.

2. What has to be in place first:
- Live jusprinv2 Chargebee is ready. I created the item prices jusprin-hobby-yearly ($100) and jusprin-workshop-yearly ($200) and the coupon jusprin1-move-first-term. I also widened jusprin2-obico-premium-20 to the yearly prices. Kenneth turned on Price override (Billing LogIQ). Live estimates check out: Workshop yearly with the Obico coupon is $160. A mover at $59.99 with the first-term coupon pays $0 now. A mover at $6.99 a month pays $6.99.
- No ConfigMap or env change. The plan list is code, in settings_ent.py.
- Migration 0004 adds two columns to jusprin_jusprinplan:
  - billed_cents: integer, nullable.
  - obico_discount: boolean, NOT NULL. Django drops the database default right after filling existing rows.
  So between the migrate and the end of the rollout, an old pod that inserts a new JusPrinPlan row fails with a NOT NULL error. Updates are fine. Two places insert rows:

  - JusPrin 2's record_subscription, for a first JusPrin 2 purchase.
  Chargebee retries failed webhooks, so a hit during the few-minute window should recover by itself. Migrate right before the rollout as usual.

3. Staging: not run. Staging is on obi.4104, which predates both commits. Local results: tsd-enterprise's jusprin tests pass (268). The real pages were rendered through Django's test client: prices monthly and yearly, Obico, on yearly Hobby, the moved customer, checkout done, billing and cancel. After a staging deploy, I suggest:

## Release

The main app release script is `prod/release.sh`. It applies only:

```text
prod/tsdweb-prod.yaml
prod/tsdws-prod.yaml
prod/tsdtasks-prod.yaml
prod/tsdrttasks-prod.yaml
```

It does not apply HPAs, services, BackendConfigs, Ingress, managed certificates,
`tsdbeat-prod`, `tsdml-api-prod`, or `flower-prod`. Apply those explicitly if
they changed.

The script also runs `git add ..`, `git commit -m "Release"`, and `git push`.
Use it only when you are ready for that commit/push behavior. For controlled
releases, prefer manual commands.

Before release:

```bash
cd ~/Projects/ops/tsd/prod
git status --short
kubectl --context=tsd get deploy,hpa,pods -n default | grep -E 'tsd|NAME'
curl -fsS https://app.obico.io/hc/
```

Update image tags in the relevant manifests:

```text
prod/tsdweb-prod.yaml
prod/tsdws-prod.yaml
prod/tsdtasks-prod.yaml
prod/tsdrttasks-prod.yaml
prod/tsdbeat-prod.yaml
prod/tsdml-api-prod.yaml
```

Manual release for web/ws/tasks:

```bash
cd ~/Projects/ops/tsd/prod

kubectl --context=tsd apply -f tsdweb-prod.yaml
kubectl --context=tsd rollout status deploy/tsdweb-prod -n default --timeout=15m
curl -fsS https://app.obico.io/hc/

kubectl --context=tsd apply -f tsdws-prod.yaml
kubectl --context=tsd rollout status deploy/tsdws-prod -n default --timeout=15m

kubectl --context=tsd apply -f tsdtasks-prod.yaml
kubectl --context=tsd rollout status deploy/tsdtasks-prod -n default --timeout=15m

kubectl --context=tsd apply -f tsdrttasks-prod.yaml
kubectl --context=tsd rollout status deploy/tsdrttasks-prod -n default --timeout=15m
```

After releasing `tsdws-prod`, the existing script waits 20 minutes and then
scales websocket replicas down by two one step at a time, with 5 minutes between
steps. This is meant to redistribute long-lived websocket connections. If doing
this manually:

```bash
kubectl --context=tsd get deploy tsdws-prod -n default -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}{"\n"}'
kubectl --context=tsd scale --replicas=<replicas-minus-1> deploy/tsdws-prod -n default
sleep 300
kubectl --context=tsd scale --replicas=<replicas-minus-2> deploy/tsdws-prod -n default
```

Manual release for ML:

```bash
cd ~/Projects/ops/tsd/prod

kubectl --context=tsd apply -f tsdml-api-prod.yaml
kubectl --context=tsd rollout status deploy/tsdml-api-prod -n default --timeout=20m
kubectl --context=tsd get pods -n default -o wide | grep tsdml-api-prod
```

The existing `prod/release-tsdml-api.md` is a short old note, not a full
runbook. It still describes the rough idea of temporarily increasing ML
capacity, but it uses the stale deployment name `tsdml-api` and the local `kb`
alias. Use explicit `kubectl --context=tsd` commands and the live deployment
name `tsdml-api-prod`.

If choosing the old HPA-disable rollout pattern for ML, use:

```bash
cd ~/Projects/ops/tsd/prod
kubectl --context=tsd delete -f tsdml-api-prod-hpa.yaml
kubectl --context=tsd scale --replicas=2 deploy/tsdml-api-prod -n default
kubectl --context=tsd rollout status deploy/tsdml-api-prod -n default --timeout=20m
kubectl --context=tsd apply -f tsdml-api-prod.yaml
kubectl --context=tsd rollout status deploy/tsdml-api-prod -n default --timeout=20m
kubectl --context=tsd apply -f tsdml-api-prod-hpa.yaml
kubectl --context=tsd get hpa tsdml-api-prod-hpa -n default
```

Only delete HPA for a specific, understood reason. The default safer path is to
apply the ML deployment and watch rollout, HPA, pods, and GPU capacity.

RED='\033[0;31m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Trap to catch errors and display in red
trap 'exit_code=$?; trap - ERR; echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! Command failed with exit code $exit_code${NC}" >&2; exit $exit_code' ERR

. $HOME/.nvm/nvm.sh

# ── Preflight checks ──

echo "Running preflight checks..."

# Ensure obico-server is on master and push
cd obico-server
BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
if [ "$BRANCH" != "master" ]; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! obico-server is on branch '$BRANCH', not 'master'. Aborting.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi
echo "Pushing obico-server..."
if ! git push; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! Failed to push obico-server. Aborting.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi
cd ..

# Ensure tsd-enterprise is on master and push
BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
if [ "$BRANCH" != "master" ]; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! tsd-enterprise is on branch '$BRANCH', not 'master'. Aborting.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi
echo "Pushing tsd-enterprise..."
if ! git push; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! Failed to push tsd-enterprise. Aborting.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi

echo "Preflight checks passed ✅"

# ── Build ──

cd obico-server/frontend
nvm use
npm ci # for some reason if node_modules folder is missing in the public repo, `npm run build` in the ent repo will fail

if ! git diff-index --quiet HEAD --; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! Local changes not commited. Aborting release.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi
git pull && git checkout master
LAST_PUB_COMMIT="$(git log -1)"
git push

cd ../..
if git diff-index HEAD -- | grep -v obico-server ; then
    echo -e "${RED}ERROR!!! Local changes not commited. Aborting release.${NC}"
    exit 1
fi

git pull && git checkout master
LAST_ENT_COMMIT="$(git log -1)"

# Recreate the release branch from master instead of rebasing
git checkout -B release master

cd web_ent/frontend && nvm use && npm ci && npm run build && cd ../..

The release has started. Its commit (`51b2fd5838`) is on tsd-enterprise's `release` branch, and CircleCI is building the server image. The commit holds the yearly plans with their database migration, the moved-customer warning, the JusPrin 1 move list and three doc changes. The front end hasn't changed, so the release reuses the last build's bundles.

Staging and production both match the ops files. The one known difference is production's websocket pods, which run 10 on purpose while the file says 12, so I'll update their image directly instead of applying the file.

Once the image appears, I'll put it on staging and check it. Then I'll ask you to buy yearly Hobby once with Chargebee's test card.
do we need to wait for the paypal checkout sesession before we release?

No, the release doesn't need to wait for the PayPal session. Its fix is only in the desktop app, and it told me it needs no server change, no Chargebee setting and no production setting.

The only overlap is staging. When I put the new image on staging, its web pod restarts and the database migration runs, so staging will be briefly unavailable. If the PayPal test ran a payment at that moment, the payment could fail. Its build still has a while to go, so I'll finish the staging rollout before then. If its test turns out to be ready first, I'll hold the staging step until the test is done.

# Home's AI card and first-run page showed an old account (fix on claude/home-account-refresh)

Branch `claude/home-account-refresh`, commit 4da941e553, worktree
/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/home-account-refresh (Release build in build/arm64).
Not pushed; waits on Kenneth.

## Causes
- OrcaHomeBackend fetched /ent/jusprin/v2/account once per app run (m_account_requested never reset),
  so the credits never changed and a later account inherited the earlier one's balance.
- ShellController::open_preferences never re-sent Home's state after the window closed, so a
  sign-out or sign-in in Preferences did not reach Home or the first-run import page until
  something else redrew Home.

## Fix
Credits are kept with the email they belong to (dropped and re-read when it changes), re-read each
time Home comes on screen, and re-read with a Home redraw when Preferences closes.

## Evidence
- Staging, real app, before the fix: k+stg-e2e1 showed "494 credits left" on Home; after one
  Standard request the server said 493; Home still said 494 after New project and back.
  Screenshot: scratchpad/evidence/credits-before-fix-home-494-server-493.jpg (session f7445e00).
- Shell harness --fresh-example (stand-in server): new checks fail without the fix (card still
  "Signed in as alex@example.com / 500 credits left" after the server dropped to 493 and after the
  real Preferences Sign out button was clicked) and pass with it. Default harness mode: 625 checks,
  0 failures. jusprin_tests: all 175 cases pass.

- Staging, real app, after the fix (2026-11-10): Home showed 493; one Standard request took the
  server to 492; File › New project and back to Home showed 492. Signing out in Preferences and
  closing the window left Home with no "Signed in as k+stg-e2e1" line. Screenshots in
  scratchpad/evidence (session f7445e00).

## Gap found by reading, not yet run
- A chat in the printer conversation panel opened from Home spends credits, but closing that panel
  does not re-read Home's balance: ShellController::on_page_changed returns early while the panel is
  open, so m_home_shown stays true and the "came back to Home" re-read never fires.

## Not done
- clang-tidy now passes (commit 29801edb15 adds a missing <utility>). To run it on this Mac: set
  CLANG_TIDY to the 22.1.8 copy in worktree adoring-chatterjee-3ad22d/build-tidy/clang-tidy-venv,
  and seed build-tidy with -DLIBLZMA_INCLUDE_DIR=/opt/homebrew/include before the script configures.
- After a sign-out, Home shows no AI group at all (home_agent_card returns None while
  jusprin_agent.enabled stays true). That predates this change.

## 2026-11-10: read-when-shown design built (commit b1ea968945, not pushed)

Kenneth approved "each credits screen reads the account from the server whenever it comes on screen". Built on claude/home-account-refresh as b1ea968945 on top of 4da941e553 and 29801edb15.

- Triggers: main window activated (back from another app, Preferences, purchase sheet), Home shown, project AI panel expanded, printer chat closed. Only the visible screen reads; no screen refreshes another.
- Shared account read drops answers for a token no longer saved (sign-out mid-read).
- Removed cross-screen refreshes: AgentUI window-focus listener, purchase sheet's pane refresh, Preferences' refresh of Home/pane.
- Verified: shell harness PASS in --fresh-example and default modes (read counts asserted per step); jusprin_tests 175 cases; AgentUI 712 tests + tsc; clang-tidy vs jusprin-dev passes. Real app on staging (k+stg-e2e1): 9 reads across startup, hide/show, Preferences open/close, new project, 6 tab clicks (0 reads), back to Home, printer chat open/close; Home showed 487 matching the server.
- Not verified: Windows and Linux main-window activation behaviour.

## Landed locally

Kenneth asked to squash: the three commits are now one commit, 2900b98fc7, on local jusprin-dev (main checkout fast-forwarded, clean). Same tree as claude/home-account-refresh tip b1ea968945. Not pushed.

Pushed to origin jusprin-dev (ed7b6810fb..2900b98fc7) with Kenneth's yes; main checkout in sync.

## Home simplified (f2322b9857, pushed to jusprin-dev)

Home drops its email tracking; it stores the token each account answer was read with and shows credits only while that token is saved. Harness both modes, jusprin_tests, clang-tidy pass. Main checkout in sync.

content.text: I've checked about 20 searches so far without finding your request. Checking one last session, the active first-launch review, before reporting.

I couldn't find where you asked for this. I searched every Claude Code session on this Mac, archived ones included, the design canvas comments and my memory notes. None of them has a request to remove Home's AI section when signed out. If you gave it in a chat outside Claude Code, a voice note or a canvas thread I couldn't reach, I can't see it from here. If you remember which session it was, I'll read exactly what it was told and what it did.

**What Home does today.** `home_agent_card()` in [OnboardingModel.cpp:42](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/OnboardingModel.cpp:42) picks Home's AI section using only two things: whether any AI is set up, and whether you're signed in. Whether you've ever signed in doesn't count.
- **No AI set up:** Home shows the "Set up AI" card from your screenshot, with Google, email and "Use your own AI account". This is the case you hit.
- **Signed in:** Home shows "Signed in as … · credits" until you press Hide.
- **Signed out after using a JusPrin account:** Home shows no AI section at all. The app still counts AI as set up after sign-out, so nothing appears. The Home credits session noticed this and left it alone.

**Why it's there.** The welcome screen's "Just slice for now" leads to Home, and this card is the only place on Home that offers sign-up again. That came from the first-run design you agreed on 2026-11-02, where Home keeps the welcome's three choices after "Just slice". Removing the card would leave Preferences › Account as the only way to sign up after skipping it.

Two questions decide the change:
- Should the card go only for someone who never signed in, or also after a sign-out?
- Should anything stay on Home as a way back to signing up, or should Preferences › Account be the only way?

Tell me what you want, and I'll have the design boards updated and the change built. It's separate from the server release, which is still waiting for CircleCI's image.

Exit code 1
---
name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.

**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.

input.title: Home: let people dismiss the Set up AI card
input.prompt:
Give Home's "Set up AI" card a way to dismiss it, and make the card stop showing for people who already use AI through an MCP tool.

How it works today (checked in code on `jusprin-dev` at 519189a293):
- `home_agent_card()` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/OnboardingModel.cpp:42` returns `Doors` (the "Set up AI" card, rendered by `HomeUI/src/components/AgentGroup.tsx` with `SignInDoor` and `OwnAccountDoor`) whenever `agent_configured` is false.
- `OrcaHomeBackend::agent_configured()` (`Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:444`) is true when `jusprin_agent.enabled == "true"` (own API key or JusPrin account) or the onboarding flag `tool_connected` is set.
- `tool_connected` is set in only one place: `open_agent_door()` (`OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:756`), when Preferences was opened from Home's card and closed with "tool". Someone who connects an MCP client from Preferences › Agent opened any other way, or who points an MCP client at the app by hand, never gets the flag, so the card stays on Home forever.
- Only the Account card has a dismiss flag (`kAccountCardDismissed`); the Set up AI card has none.

What to do:
1. Read `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, `design-guidelines.md` and `design-system.md`. Update the design boards first (the Home board on the JusPrin v2 canvas artifact) with a dismiss control on the card and where it goes afterwards; show Kenneth the board and get his yes before building.
2. Record an MCP connection wherever the app learns of one (Preferences › Agent's tool setup, and if practical the MCP server seeing a client connect), not only from Home's door.
3. Add the dismiss: a saved flag like `kAccountCardDismissed`, a page action, and a way back (Preferences › Agent already holds setup). Add tests in the existing OnboardingModel tests and the HomeUI tests.
4. Kenneth also has open questions on whether the card should hide after a sign-out; ask him in full rather than deciding.
Done: boards approved, the change built and tested on the real app on macOS, committed on a branch from `jusprin-dev`; ask Kenneth how to land it.

Kenneth saw the "Set up AI" card on Home and said it is very annoying if it keeps showing to people who set up their own API key or use MCP, and that there should at least be a way to dismiss it. Own API key already hides it; MCP only hides it in the one path above. Follow AGENTS.md (UI token rules, wording rules, fork-stewardship before touching OrcaSlicer-owned files). Another session is coordinating a server release; this change is app-only and does not touch the server.

"""What JusPrin 2 sells through Chargebee, and the credits each sale grants.

JusPrin 2 sells on a Chargebee site of its own (JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_SITE),
apart from Obico's (CHARGEBEE_SITE), so its checkout, emails and invoices are
JusPrin's. Every call here passes that site; the module never uses the site
chargebee.configure() set for Obico. The site is on Chargebee's Product Catalog
2.0, so a plan or the pack is an item price and is bought with the *_for_items
calls.

The credit pack is a one-off charge (JUSPRIN_V2_PACK_PRICE_ID) bought on a
one-time checkout; its lot never expires. Hobby and Workshop are Chargebee
plans whose item price ids are JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS' keys; a monthly plan's term
grants a lot that expires with the term. A yearly plan's term grants a lot a
month: the first when the year is paid, each later one lazily from
ensure_lots once its month has begun, each expiring when its month ends. Until
JUSPRIN_V2_LAUNCH_OFFER_ENDS every lot comes with a launch-bonus lot of the same
size and expiry; a later month's bonus follows when that month began.

A lot is keyed by the invoice or the term that paid for it, so the checkout's
return and Chargebee's webhook can both report one sale and it counts once.

A JusPrin 2 account is a Chargebee customer of its own, jusprinv2-<user id>
(JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_CUSTOMER_PREFIX names the prefix),
apart from any Obico account with the same email (lib/syndicate.py),
so the webhook finds the account by that id and never by email.
"""

def _when(seconds) -> Optional[datetime]:

def _grant(user_id: int, kind: str, credits: int, source_ref: str, expires_at: Optional[datetime],
           earned_at: datetime = None) -> bool:
    """Grants a lot, and the launch bonus beside it when the lot was earned while
    the launch was on (now, unless earned_at says when). False when the lot was
    granted before."""
    lot = {'kind': kind, 'credits_granted': credits, 'credits_remaining': credits, 'expires_at': expires_at}
    with transaction.atomic():
        _, made = CreditGrant.objects.get_or_create(user_id=user_id, source_ref=source_ref, defaults=lot)
        if made and launch_on(earned_at):

    return made

    """What the lots of the plan's current term are keyed by. A yearly term's
    first month is keyed by this alone, month n (from 0) by '<term_ref>:<n>'."""
    return f'term:{plan.external_id}:{plan.plan_id}:{int(plan.current_term_start.timestamp())}'

On 2026-11-02 evening, after seeing canvas version 73, Kenneth corrected the credits design in four ways:

- Every credit is the same. No Standard-only ("basic_only", "trickle") lot. Free accounts (not subscribed) get 50 credits a month, expiring one month after grant, that pay for either tier. Not "everyone": he told the design session "the 'everyone gets 50 credits' wording is wrong. I never said that." I had told the design session "yes, everyone" as my own pick before he answered; never pass my pick on as his. His words: "let's just give free users 50/mo use-it-or-loose it credits".
- Workshop has no ceiling. "no ceiling. It's probably easier just to say standard messages cost 0 credits". Nothing about 600 or fair use remains.
- A balance is one number of credits, never "N Standard or N Expert messages" beside it ("showing a number of messages and credits at the same time is fucking confusing"). The translation line was my addition in the design doc, never his decision. Bars are grouped only by expiry; bought credits get a bar too (decision 13 closed).
- "New Standard chat" and board 3d are gone, since the case only existed because of the Standard-only lot.

Prices in messages appear only where the person chooses or is stopped: picker options, the stop card for the chat's tier, the pricing page's one sentence, the low-balance notice, and one scale line under the first-month offer.

**Why:** he said he was "seriously worried that we are not on the same page" and asked me to restate the plan; the Standard-only lot and the ceiling were placeholders the plan carried without his words behind them.

**How to apply:** before presenting any credits surface, check it against these four. When a plan carries a mechanism (a lot kind, a cap) with no quote from Kenneth behind it, flag it as mine rather than drawing it on every board. Related: [[credit-price-needs-its-unit]], [[usage-against-quota-common-shape]], [[trace-a-rule-to-kenneths-words]].

Later the same evening Kenneth reviewed every mechanism that was mine, not his. Kept: the launch offer, "About 25 credits left" (credits, not messages), "Expiring credits are used first", the savings switch on by default, the Account page shape, Standard as the default tier after the first month, the v1 welcome-back fill-ins, the print-report form details, the alias ids. Dropped: the reverse savings alert and board 7c, the month-end and 7-day expiry notices, the daily cap on free app turns, the thinking picker on Standard. Expiry: every expiring lot expires one month from the day it was granted, never at a calendar month end. His message was only a keep list, so anything left off it counts as dropped. A session wrongly called the report rules "neither kept nor dropped"; he corrected that the same day: "I thought the clawback are removed, rigth? And why is it still a placeholder?" The clawback is removed. Asked about 25 credits, three a day and stopping after two invalid reports, he ruled: "Remove these. only keep the 1st one". A report earns 25 credits, one per G-code, and a review is only recorded.

Ruled later: "no 50 credits for first month. only 500 initial credits. pack holders also get 50 credits a month." The 50 a month goes to every account not on a subscription, starting after the first month; the balance example is 62 + 500 = 562 with no Free credits bar.

**What was wrong.** Until February 1, the server doubles every credit pack and every plan's credits ("Double credits on everything"). It does this by adding a second, equal batch of credits that expires at the same time as the first. The app had no name for those extra batches. So each one showed up as its own bar, labeled only "Credits". Your yearly Hobby plan showed as "Hobby credits 750" plus an unnamed "Credits 750". Your packs showed as "Bought credits 1,000" plus an unnamed "Credits 1,000". The amounts were right, but nothing explained the second bars.

- Sign-up credits: 471 of 500 left, expires 9 Dec
- Hobby credits: 1,500 of 1,500 left. Expires 11 Dec. Doubled for the launch. Unused credits don't carry over.
- Bought credits: 3,000 of 3,000 left. Never expire. Doubled for the launch.

The total went from 3,971 to 4,971 because staging recorded a third pack purchase at 15:12 UTC today. I assume that was you or the PayPal test.

The sign-up date reads 9 Dec here but read 10 Dec in your screenshot. The credits expire at 00:40 UTC on 10 Dec, which is still 9 Dec on Pacific time. My guess is that your screenshot came from a machine set to UTC, such as the Windows test machine.

**Where it applies.** The same bars appear in three places: the Home card, the credits panel next to the chat box, and Preferences › Account. All three use the fix.

**Testing.**
- I added a test using your account's exact credit batches. It failed on the old code with the same five bars as your screenshot, and it passes now.
- All other tests pass: 716 for the Agent page and 162 for Home.

content.text:
You're right, my app fix depends on a guess, and I'd go with your simpler option.

**What my fix does.** When someone buys something, the server stores two separate batches of credits: the purchase itself, and a launch bonus of the same size. It doesn't record which purchase a bonus belongs to. So the app guesses from the expiry date. A bonus that never expires is counted with the bought packs, and a bonus that expires is counted with the plan. That's right today only because the server doubles packs and plans and nothing else. If the server ever doubled something else, such as the credits for a print report, the app would put that bonus in the wrong bar without any error. The fix also added the "Doubled for the launch" note. It's about 25 lines, and it isn't robust.

**Your option.** While the launch offer runs, the server stores one batch of twice the size. A Hobby month becomes a single batch of 1,500 credits, and a pack becomes a single batch of 1,000. The app needs no special handling, and the bar reads "Hobby credits 1,500 of 1,500 left. Expires 11 Dec. Unused credits don't carry over." The server change is about one line in the code that grants credits, plus updating its tests. Here's what I checked:
- **Production:** it has no bonus batches yet, only two sign-up batches. There's nothing to convert.
- **Staging:** your test account has four bonus batches. I'd fold each one into its purchase with a one-off database fix, so your card shows the same three bars.
- **Pages that say "doubled":** the Credits and plans page and the purchase confirmation page decide what to say from the launch dates, not from these batches. They keep working unchanged.

**Decision needed: should the server grant one doubled batch, with the app fix dropped?** It's your call, because it removes the app commit and needs another server release. Here are the options:
- **Yes (my pick).** I'd remove my app commit, af8b836bb6. It's only on your local `jusprin-dev` and was never pushed. I'd also change the server, fix the four staging batches, and release to staging and then production, about 15 minutes each. The app stays untouched.
- **Keep the app fix.** No new release, but the app keeps a guess that only holds while the server doubles packs and plans alone.

Do you want me to go ahead with the server change?
Yes, do it

content.text:
Your credits card is now simple. During the launch, the server gives each pack or plan month a single batch of twice the credits, so the app needs no special rule. I sent you a screenshot of Home on your staging account, from the app with no changes of mine:

- **5,971 credits left**
- **Sign-up credits:** 471 of 500 left. Expires 9 Dec.
- **Hobby credits:** 1,500 of 1,500 left. Expires 11 Dec. Unused credits don't carry over.
- **Bought credits:** 4,000 of 4,000 left. Never expire.

There's no "Doubled for the launch" line and no unnamed bars. The bought total is 4,000 because staging has four 500-credit packs on your account, each doubled.

**What changed:**
- **App:** I dropped my earlier app fix. It was never pushed, so `jusprin-dev` is back where GitHub has it.
- **Server:** the credit-granting code now doubles the amount while the launch offer runs, instead of adding a separate bonus batch. I also removed the bonus credit type and the code that handled it. All 272 JusPrin server tests pass. The change is on master as ae96b797cd.
- **Staging:** the database had 11 old bonus batches across your test accounts. I added each one into the purchase it doubled, then deleted it.
- **Production:** it had no bonus batches, so there was nothing to convert.
- **Release:** staging and production run server build obi.4113. The health check returns 200 on all three hosts, and Sentry shows no new errors. The ops change is pushed, and the PayPal session knows the release hold is lifted.

**Is the code simpler?** The code I wrote is shorter: 14 lines added and 21 removed. On top of that, Django generated an 18-line database migration file, so the whole commit adds 11 more lines than it removes. That file exists only because I removed the bonus credit type from the list of allowed types. It changes no tables or data. The alternative was to leave the unused type in the list and skip the file. Removing it seemed cleaner than keeping a type nothing uses, but if you'd rather avoid the file, I can undo that part.

content.text:
Yes, that line is a special rule. The app adds "Unused credits don't carry over" only to a bar that holds plan credits, and sign-up credits never get it (`BalancePanel.tsx:38`). It doesn't change how credits work, though. Sign-up credits also disappear on their expiry date. The line just repeats what "Expires 11 Dec" already says.

Your rule already matches what the server does. It spends the credits that expire soonest first and the ones that never expire last. I checked the order in the server's spending code at `ledger.py:80`.

Going through the credit bars, here is everything that isn't plain "how many left, and when they expire":

- **The carry-over line on plan credits.** This is the only special rule. Removing it is a one-line change in the app, plus its test. Each bar would then show just "Expires 11 Dec" or "Never expire".
- **The bar names: Sign-up, Hobby, Bought.** These only label where the credits came from. Nothing behaves differently by name, so I'd keep them.
- **"Expiring credits are used first."** This shows under the bars when there are two or more. It states your rule, so I'd keep it.
- **The prices page's Hobby and Workshop cards** say "These credits reset each month. Unused ones don't carry over." That tells someone what they're buying before they pay, so I'd leave it. It isn't part of the bars.

My proposal is to remove the carry-over line from the bars and leave the rest as it is. The change goes on `jusprin-dev` in the app. Nothing on the server changes, and nothing has been changed yet.

content.text:
I pushed the credit bar fix to `jusprin-dev`. There was only one credit-bar commit in the app, 5f4de64e6b, so there was nothing to squash. The launch-bonus app fix I made earlier was dropped before it was ever pushed.

The server side of the release is done. The next step, the team installing JusPrin 2, is blocked: there's no signed build of `jusprin-dev` to install.

## Where the release stands

**Server: done and live.**
- Production runs server build obi.4113 on `app.obico.io` and `jusprinv2.obico.io`.
- It has the monthly and yearly Hobby and Workshop plans, credit packs, the Obico subscriber discount, the warning for moved JusPrin 1 customers, and the JusPrin 1 move list.
- Launch credits are stored as one doubled batch.
- Health checks pass and Sentry shows no new errors.

**Payments: tested on staging, still one check owed on production.**
- Card checkout works on staging: credit packs, monthly plans, and your yearly Hobby purchase.
- The PayPal fix is on `jusprin-dev`. The PayPal session made real sandbox payments with it on Mac, Windows and Linux.
- Your real-card credit pack purchase on production hasn't happened yet. It's the only check that proves live payments end to end.

**App: features are in, but no build to install.**
- `jusprin-dev` has today's fixes: the Set up AI card's "Don't show again", the credit bars, Skip for now, and PayPal.
- The automatic nightly build of `jusprin-dev` failed on November 10 and again today.
  - On both days, the macOS jobs never got a machine to run on and were cancelled after about 95 minutes.
  - Today the Linux job also failed, because GitHub's build machine couldn't reach Ubuntu's package server.
  - My guess is that this build competes for macOS machines with the `main` build that starts at the same minute. I haven't checked that.
- `main` is 14 commits behind `jusprin-dev`. That's expected: `main` only moves forward when a version is released.

## Next steps, in order

1. **Get the nightly build passing.** Without it, nobody can install the current app. I've put up a task card for it: [Get the jusprin-dev nightly build passing again](#task_c8ad5d63).
2. **Your real-card credit pack purchase on production.** You can do it with the signed build once step 1 works, or now with the local build pointed at production if you want it sooner.
3. **Decide on Chargebee receipts.** They're off on both the live and test Chargebee sites, so buyers get no email receipt.
4. **Team round.** Everyone on the team installs the signed build, signs in against production, and uses it for real for a few days.
5. **Review the 2.0.0 release notes** (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/2.0.0.md`) against what shipped since they were written: yearly plans, the launch offer and PayPal. Then build the signed 2.0.0 release.
6. **Publish 2.0.0 and send emails in waves:** hand-picked testers first, then JusPrin 1 users (moving their subscriptions with the move list), then Obico users.

One known gap remains. PayPal declined to let Chargebee save PayPal accounts for repeat billing, so paying for a monthly or yearly plan with PayPal will likely fail. One-time pack purchases with PayPal work. Either take this up with PayPal, or say at checkout that plans need a card.

The [nightly build session](#local_85d6fc0f-9739-485a-a6c5-cb976c6afbea) found why the `jusprin-dev` nightly fails. A retry script is running, and the session needs one decision from you.

**Why it fails.** GitHub won't give this repository an Apple-silicon Mac to build on during US daytime. The nightly is set for 07:35 UTC, but GitHub starts every scheduled workflow in this repository 7 to 10 hours late, which lands it in exactly those hours. If a job gets no machine within 15 minutes, GitHub cancels it. The session tested this at 17:47 UTC:
- Apple-silicon Macs got no machine.
- Intel Macs got one in 6 seconds.
- Builds that started between 22:00 and 08:30 UTC always got Apple-silicon machines.

OrcaSlicer's own builds got machines in the same hour. The session's guess, not confirmed, is that GitHub serves free-plan accounts last. Others have reported the same problem since about November 2 on GitHub's community forum, with no answer from GitHub. The session ruled out three other causes: competition with `main`'s build, billing, and our own limit on Mac jobs.

**Getting a build for the team now.** A script re-runs the failed Mac jobs every 30 minutes. It stops when the build succeeds, on a real build error, or after 18 hours. The session expects success after about 22:00 UTC (14:00 Pacific). A successful run updates the `nightly-builds` pre-release, which is what the team would install.

**Already written, not pushed.** Commit 05c9e48de1 on `claude/nightly-macos-runners` moves one small step, looking up the Mac dependency cache, onto a Linux machine, as OrcaSlicer does. A nightly then needs three Mac machines instead of five. It hasn't run in a real build yet.

**Decision needed: how should the nightly avoid this from now on?** It's yours because two of the options touch `main` or cost money.
- **Retry automatically.** A small workflow re-runs a nightly whose Mac jobs got no machine. It's free. GitHub only runs that kind of workflow from `main`'s copy of the file, so `main` would need to change, which needs your yes.
- **Use Intel Macs where possible.** It's free, but the Intel dependencies would be rebuilt once, Intel machines are slower, and GitHub stops offering them around fall 2027.
- **Use paid Mac machines.** You'd raise the GitHub spending limit. The session estimates about $20 a night but hasn't checked that number.

The session recommends the automatic retry, together with the cache-lookup commit, and I agree. Answer it in [its session](#local_85d6fc0f-9739-485a-a6c5-cb976c6afbea).

The session expects the retries to reach a green build after about 22:00 UTC (14:00 Pacific), going by when Macs were available on earlier days. The retry hasn't run in a real nightly yet; its first real test comes at about 19:50 UTC. If retries keep failing, the session has a fallback ready: register this Mac as a build machine.
