result.output:
JusPrin 2 is a new app, not an update of JusPrin 1. It is built on OrcaSlicer 2.5.0, and every project has AI working beside it. You tell AI what you are printing and what went wrong. AI reads your file, your settings and your slice, changes the settings and slices again.

## What AI can do

Each project has an AI chat beside the 3D view. Ask in plain words, and AI works in the open project:

- Set up the printer, filament and print settings for the part you are printing.
- Open a model or project file, place objects on the plate, and lay out plates.
- Cut, split, merge and repair objects.
- Change print settings for you.
- Slice the plate and check the result, for example support printed inside a hole, or a part that starts in the air.
- Look at a photo of a failed print and suggest what to change.
- Run a filament calibration test (temperature, flow or pressure advance), read a photo of the printed test, and save the result as a new filament preset.

When you ask AI to print, it opens the usual send dialog. You choose the options and press Send. AI never starts a print.

When a slice has a problem, a marker on the 3D view shows it. Press Ask AI to have AI explain the problem and your options.

## Ways to use AI

- Sign up for a JusPrin account in the app. New accounts get free credits, and no card is needed.
- Use your own OpenAI, Anthropic or OpenRouter API key.
- Connect an AI app you already use: Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop or Cursor. It can then work with the project open in JusPrin.
- Or skip AI and just slice.

## Also new

- **Home screen.** Your projects and printers are on one screen. Each printer card shows the printer's status, and opens the printer's own window.
- **Printers.** Add a printer and connect it by chatting with AI. Bambu Lab, Klipper (Moonraker) and OctoPrint printers can be connected.
- **Saving.** Projects save themselves, so JusPrin never asks you to save or discard. File › Save (Cmd+S on a Mac, Ctrl+S on Windows and Linux) keeps a version you can go back to in File › Version history. Saving doesn't write over the .3mf file you opened. To get a .3mf file, use File › Export › Project 3MF (Cmd+Shift+S or Ctrl+Shift+S).
- **Opening files.** A file you open from Finder or File Explorer opens as a new project. A model dropped on the 3D view is added to the open project.
- **Check print.** Print › Check print shows a report of the slice beside the preview.
- **Print history.** Every sliced file you export or send to a printer is listed on Home's Print history, and you can print it again from there.
- **Classic view.** View › Switch to classic view shows OrcaSlicer's full interface. Press Back to JusPrin to return.
- **Updates.** JusPrin checks its GitHub releases for a new version once a day. You see the result in Preferences › Updates.
- **Reporting a problem.** Help › Report a problem opens a new GitHub issue in your browser, with the app's version and your system filled in.

## Upgrading from JusPrin 1.4

- **Installing.** On Windows, the installer replaces JusPrin 1. On a Mac, JusPrin 2 is also called JusPrin.app, so dragging it to Applications replaces JusPrin 1. On Linux, the AppImage is a new file, and JusPrin 1's AppImage stays where it is.
- **Your printers.** The first time JusPrin 2 starts, it offers to import your printers from JusPrin 1 or OrcaSlicer, with their filaments and print settings. You choose which printers to import. You can import later with File › Import › Import from JusPrin 1 or Import from OrcaSlicer.
- **Your JusPrin 1 folder.** JusPrin 2 keeps its settings in a new folder. It only reads JusPrin 1's folder and never changes it. JusPrin 1's app settings, such as units and language, aren't imported.
- **Your account.** Your JusPrin 1 sign-in doesn't carry over. To use AI with a JusPrin account, sign up in JusPrin 2, even if you had an account in JusPrin 1. Chats from JusPrin 1 aren't imported.

## Downloads

- **Windows (64-bit):** the installer, or the portable .zip, which runs without installing.
- **Mac:** one disk image for Macs with Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
- **Linux (64-bit):** an AppImage, built on Ubuntu 24.04. Make the file executable, then run it.
- **SHA256SUMS.txt** lists each file's checksum.

Questions or problems: write to jusprin-support@obico.io, or use Help › Report a problem in the app.

JusPrin 2 is a new app, not an update of JusPrin 1. It is built on OrcaSlicer 2.5.0, and every project has AI working beside it. You tell AI what you are printing and what went wrong. AI reads your file, your settings and your slice, changes the settings and slices again.

## What AI can do

Each project has an AI chat beside the 3D view. Ask in plain words, and AI works in the open project:

- Set up the printer, filament and print settings for the part you are printing.
- Open a model or project file, place objects on the plate, and lay out plates.
- Cut, split, merge and repair objects.
- Change print settings for you.
- Slice the plate and check the result, for example support printed inside a hole, or a part that starts in the air.
- Look at a photo of a failed print and suggest what to change.
- Run a filament calibration test (temperature, flow or pressure advance), read a photo of the printed test, and save the result as a new filament preset.

When you ask AI to print, it opens the usual send dialog. You choose the options and press Send. AI never starts a print.

When a slice has a problem, a marker on the 3D view shows it. Press Ask AI to have AI explain the problem and your options.

## Ways to use AI

- Sign up for a JusPrin account in the app. New accounts get free credits, and no card is needed.
- Use your own OpenAI, Anthropic or OpenRouter API key.
- Connect an AI app you already use: Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop, Cowork, Cursor or VS Code. It can then work with the project open in JusPrin.
- Or skip AI and just slice.

## Also new

- **Home screen.** Your projects and printers are on one screen. Each printer card shows the printer's status, and once the printer is connected, opens its own window.
- **Printers.** Add a printer and connect it by chatting with AI. You can connect Bambu Lab printers in LAN mode, and Klipper (Moonraker) and OctoPrint printers.
- **Saving.** Projects save themselves, so JusPrin never asks you to save or discard. File › Save (Cmd+S on a Mac, Ctrl+S on Windows and Linux) keeps a version you can go back to in File › Version history. Saving doesn't write over the .3mf file you opened. To get a .3mf file, use File › Export › Project 3MF (Cmd+Shift+S or Ctrl+Shift+S).
- **Opening files.** A file you open from Finder or File Explorer opens as a new project. A model dropped on the 3D view is added to the open project.
- **Check print.** Print › Check print shows a report of the slice beside the preview.
- **Print history.** Every sliced file you export or send to a printer is listed on Home's Print history, and you can print it again from there.
- **Classic view.** View › Switch to classic view shows OrcaSlicer's full interface. Press Back to JusPrin to return.
- **Updates.** JusPrin checks its GitHub releases for a new version once a day. You see the result in Preferences › Updates.
- **Reporting a problem.** Help › Report a problem opens a new GitHub issue in your browser, with the app's version and your system filled in.

## Upgrading from JusPrin 1.4

- **Installing.** On Windows, the installer replaces JusPrin 1. On a Mac, JusPrin 2 is also called JusPrin.app, so dragging it to Applications replaces JusPrin 1. On Linux, the AppImage is a new file, and JusPrin 1's AppImage stays where it is.
- **Your printers.** The first time JusPrin 2 starts, it offers to import your printers from JusPrin 1 or OrcaSlicer, with their filaments and print settings. You choose which printers to import. You can import later with File › Import › Import from JusPrin 1 or Import from OrcaSlicer.
- **Your JusPrin 1 folder.** JusPrin 2 keeps its settings in a new folder. It only reads JusPrin 1's folder and never changes it. JusPrin 1's app settings, such as units and language, aren't imported.
- **Your account.** Your JusPrin 1 sign-in doesn't carry over. To use AI with a JusPrin account, sign up in JusPrin 2, even if you had an account in JusPrin 1. Chats from JusPrin 1 aren't imported.

## Downloads

- **Windows (64-bit):** the installer, or the portable .zip, which runs without installing.
- **Mac:** one disk image for Macs with Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
- **Linux (64-bit):** an AppImage, built on Ubuntu 24.04. Make the file executable, then run it.
- **SHA256SUMS.txt** lists each file's checksum.

Questions or problems: write to jusprin-support@obico.io, or use Help › Report a problem in the app.

name: JusPrin nightly

# Builds jusprin-dev, the development branch, once a day and puts the files
# on the "nightly-builds" pre-release, replacing the day before's, as
# JusPrin 1's "Build all" did.
#
# - GitHub runs scheduled workflows only on the default branch, main. The
#   scheduled run therefore only starts this workflow again on jusprin-dev,
#   so every step, OrcaSlicer's dependency build included, checks out
#   jusprin-dev.
# - The build is the release's (jusprin_build_all.yml), so a nightly is what a
#   release from the same commit would be. Its version is the one in
#   src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp.
# - The files keep JusPrin 1's nightly names, so download links stay the
#   same: JusPrin_Windows_Installer_nightly.exe,
#   JusPrin_Windows_nightly_portable.zip, JusPrin_Mac_universal_nightly.dmg,
#   JusPrin_Linux_AppImage_Ubuntu2404_nightly.AppImage, and SHA256SUMS.txt.
# - The nightly-builds tag moves to the commit built, and the release notes
#   name it. The scheduled build is skipped when jusprin-dev has not changed
#   since the last nightly.
# - The macOS app is signed and notarised; Windows builds are unsigned.
# - The app's update check never offers a nightly: it reads only tags named
#   vX.Y.Z and jusprin/vX.Y.Z (ReleaseFeed.cpp).
# - GitHub's hosted Apple-silicon macOS runners are often all taken in US
#   daytime, and GitHub cancels a job that gets none within 15 minutes. The
#   scheduled run lands in those hours, because this repo's schedules start
#   hours late. A run whose only failures are such jobs starts the nightly
#   again, up to 8 runs a day for one commit.
#
# Run it by hand from Actions > JusPrin nightly > Run workflow, with the
# branch set to jusprin-dev.

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '35 7 * * *' # near midnight US Pacific time, as JusPrin 1's nightly
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sign_macos:
        description: 'Sign and notarise the macOS app with the Apple secrets'
        type: boolean

# Builds JusPrin from one commit and uploads the files to a DRAFT GitHub
# release. It never publishes anything.
#
# - The version is the one in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp, and
#   the draft is tagged jusprin/v<version>, as JusPrin 1.4.0 was (the repo
#   still holds OrcaSlicer's own v2.x tags). GitHub creates that tag only when
#   the draft is published, by hand, on the Releases page. JusPrin's update
#   check reads the public release list, which never includes drafts, so
#   users see nothing until then.
# - It stops if that version is already released, is not above every
#   released JusPrin version, or its tag already exists
#   (Packaging/release.mjs), and if
#   Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md, the notes the draft starts with and
#   that the app shows under "What's new", is missing.
# - It also stops if the guide was not checked for this version
#   (docs/guide/checked-version.txt, written by scripts/check_guide.py
#   --ask-ai; see docs/guide/README.md), unless "Release without the guide
#   check" is ticked. Then the draft's title says the guide was not checked.
# - Running it again for the same version replaces the draft's files.
# - Files: Windows x64 installer and portable zip, macOS universal disk image,
#   Linux x64 AppImage, and SHA256SUMS.txt.
# - Only the release publisher can run it: the repo variable

## Before a release

The guide is brought in line with the app before each release, on a computer with the app built.

1. Build the app's test harness and pages from the commit to release: the `shell_integration_harness` and `jusprin_web` targets.
2. Leave the computer alone and run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai`. It takes about a minute a page, plus the questions.
3. Fix what it reports, then run it again until it passes:
   - **A label is on no screen.** The app's wording changed. Find the new wording in the app and correct the page.
   - **A run failed.** Open its log, which the command names. Either the screen no longer works as the page says, and the page needs correcting, or the harness expects something the app no longer does, and the harness needs correcting.
   - **A picture is blank.** The program that started the command may not record the screen. Grant it Screen Recording in the system's privacy settings and run again.
   - **AI answered a question wrongly.** Read its reply in the output. Usually the page is unclear or its first line does not say when to read it.
4. Look through what changed on screen since the last release (`git log <last release tag>..HEAD -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin`). The command finds what a page gets wrong. It cannot find a new screen or menu item that no page mentions, so add those by hand.
5. Commit the pages together with their pictures, the skills the command rebuilt, and `checked-version.txt`. When every step passes for every page, the command writes the app's version to that file. A run with `--skip-app`, with `--area`, or without `--ask-ai` leaves it as it was. The release workflow refuses a version this file does not name. The file says the check passed for that version, not on which commit, so run it on the commit you mean to release.

I cancelled the nightly build I had started for the team (GitHub Actions run 43128643231). The plan to have the team test first, then hand-picked testers, was never written in a file. I searched the JusPrin, server and ops repos, the obico.io announcement draft, your artifacts, scheduled tasks and memory, and it appears only in session chats. So there was nothing to remove. I saved a memory that the 2.0.0 rollout has no nightly or team testing, so future sessions won't suggest it again.

**Can you test the release build before publishing? Yes.** `jusprin_release.yml` never publishes anything. It builds the Windows installer and portable zip, the Mac disk image and the Linux AppImage, then uploads them to a **draft** GitHub release. Only people with write access to the repo can see a draft. The app's update check never sees drafts, and the `jusprin/v2.0.0` tag doesn't exist until you press Publish on the Releases page. You download the files from the draft, test them, and publish when you're happy. If you find a bug, fix it and run the workflow again; it replaces the draft's files.

**Two things before I can start the release build:**

1. **Moving `main` forward.** Releases are built from `main`, which is 24 commits behind `jusprin-dev`. A plain fast-forward works, so nothing is rewritten. You said earlier that `main` moves only with your yes. Your answer to the guide check question will also tell me how to start the release build, so you don't need to answer this one separately: once you pick one, I'll fast-forward `main` to `jusprin-dev`, push it, and start the workflow on `main` with Mac signing on.

2. **The guide check (the question in the box).** The release workflow stops unless `docs/guide/checked-version.txt` says 2.0.0, and that file doesn't exist yet. The guide is the set of help pages that AI reads to answer "how do I…" questions.
   - **Run the check (my pick):** I build the test harness and the AI and Home pages, then run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai`. That takes about a minute a page for eight pages, plus the questions, and the Mac has to be left alone while it captures screenshots. It may find pages that are out of date and need fixing before the release. It runs through the Claude command-line tool.
   - **Skip the check:** tick "Release without the guide check". The build starts right away, and the draft's title says the guide wasn't checked. The risk is that AI gives wrong how-to answers wherever the guide no longer matches the app.

1. **Walks the app and takes the pictures.** `tests/shell/guide_checks.json` names, for each page, the runs of the app's test harness that go through the screens the page describes, and the checks in each run the page depends on. `tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py` runs them in the app as built and copies the pictures a page uses into `pictures/<page>/`.
2. **Rebuilds the copy AI reads.** `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/guide.ts` builds a skill from each page.
3. **Checks each page**, in `guide.test.ts` beside it: every label in bold is in the app's source, every section has a run in step 1, every picture is one step 1 took, and the page has questions for step 4. `components/Guide.test.tsx` checks that the app's guide window lists every page and shows each with all its pictures and without the parts written for AI.
4. **Asks AI the page's questions** (`--ask-ai`). `tests/project_prompt/guide_questions.json` holds them with what a right answer says. `tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py` asks the model and has a judge read the replies.

## Writing a page

- Start it with `<!-- ai-description: … -->`: one line, at most 300 bytes, saying when AI should read it. The model reads every page's description together in one list, and the Claude command-line tool that `--ask-ai` runs through cuts a tool description longer than about 2,000 characters, so keep each one short: about 200 bytes. Write `...` rather than `…` in it, since that tool rewrites the one as the other.
- Put words that are only for AI in `<!-- ai: … -->`. They are hidden on this site.
- Use bold only for words that are on screen, exactly as they are on screen.
- A picture goes on a line of its own, as `![what it shows](pictures/<page>/<name>.png)`, and comes from a run named in `guide_checks.json`. AI's copy leaves it out.
- A picture is kept at twice the screen's size, and the guide window shows it at half, the size it has on screen. Mark a run's picture that the harness draws at the screen's own size with `"atScreenSize": true`, and the command doubles it.
- List a new page at the top of this file, or the guide window leaves it out.
- Give each `##` section a run in `guide_checks.json`.
- Add at least three questions for the page to `guide_questions.json`.
- AI's copy may hold at most 16 KiB. Split a page that grows past that.

---
name: windows-gui-test-vm-gcp
description: Working recipe for testing the OrcaSlicer/JusPrin GUI headlessly on a GPU-less Windows VM in GCP, and the four traps that make it fail silently.
metadata:
  type: project
---

A Windows GUI test VM for this app works in GCP with no GPU. Instance
`jusprin-win-test`, project `elegoo-backend`, zone `us-central1-a`,
n2-standard-16 (16 vCPU, 64 GB, Cascade Lake), 500 GB pd-balanced,
Windows Server 2022. Harness + full README live outside the repo
at `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/vm-harness/windows/`. Verified 2026-09-07 end to end:
launch, screenshot, scripted click, verify the UI advanced.

**Why:** four failure modes here are silent — they look like "the app has no
window" or "the app hung" rather than reporting an error, so they cost hours if
rediscovered from scratch.

**How to apply:**
- OpenGL: the app hard-requires 3.2 and Windows software rendering is 1.1. Drop
  Mesa's `opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` beside the .exe. Then force
  `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` — otherwise Mesa picks
  its d3d12 backend (the GCE virtual display exposes a D3D12 device) and crashes
  on the first frame.
- Never copy the whole Mesa .7z to the VM: Defender deletes it as
  Trojan:Win32/Suschil!rfn. Extract the two DLLs elsewhere, copy only those, and
  no AV exclusion is needed.
- Session isolation is the big one: display APIs, EnumWindows and
  MainWindowTitle only see the calling session's window station, so over SSH they
  report nothing and it reads as "no window exists". Run anything UI-touching as a
  scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive`.
- Auto-logon must be re-applied on every boot; the GCE image clears the Winlogon
  values after the boot that sets them.
- Resolution needs `gcloud compute instances update --enable-display-device`
  (instance must be stopped) or you get 640x480, smaller than the app's own window.
- WebView2 runtime is absent on a clean Windows Server image; without it the app
  blocks on a modal prompt at startup. Matters especially for JusPrin's
  WebView-based UI. See [[jusprin-rebrand-seams]].

Claude Code and the Claude desktop app are both installed for `guitest`
(2026-09-08). CLI: the native Windows installer `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1`
puts `claude.exe` in `C:\Users\guitest\.local\bin` - no Node needed, the box has
none. Desktop app: install with Anthropic's own Intune script,
`https://downloads.claude.ai/releases/enterprise/intune/Install-Claude.ps1 -Scope User`,
which resolves the official MSIX and verifies its signature and publisher identity.
MSIX deployment works on this Windows Server 2022 image. Launch the packaged app in
session 1 through explorer.exe, so it lands at normal integrity even though the
scheduled task is elevated:
`Invoke-InSession -Exe C:\Windows\explorer.exe -ArgLine "shell:AppsFolder\Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc!Claude"`.
Electron renders fine on this GPU-less VM with no flags.

RDP: port 3389 is open project-wide via `default-allow-rdp` (to 0.0.0.0/0 - not
narrowed yet), and RDP as `guitest` reconnects to the existing console session
rather than starting a second one. Run `./get-rdp-password.sh` in the harness to
print the current credentials; it resolves the ephemeral IP itself and verifies
the password actually authenticates before handing it to you. Do NOT use
`gcloud compute reset-windows-password` - autologon.ps1 re-syncs the account to
Winlogon\DefaultPassword at the next boot and would undo it.

autologon.ps1 used to mint a NEW random password on every boot, so any reboot
silently invalidated the RDP credentials. Fixed 2026-09-09: it now reuses the
stored DefaultPassword and only generates one when that value is absent (delete
the value and reboot to rotate deliberately). This matters because Windows
Update on this VM is set to install and restart on its own, daily at 3 AM, and
the box has also rebooted unexpectedly several times - Kernel-Power event 41,
cause not established.

Two mechanical traps: nested quoting through `winssh.sh` into `powershell -Command`
mangles almost anything non-trivial - write a .ps1, scp it, run it with `-File`.
And a PATH change made over SSH does not reach session 1's already-running Explorer;
re-set the variable from inside the session and restart Explorer, or a new terminal
there still will not find the command.

Tuned 2026-09-08, both changes measured. Windows Defender had real-time scanning
on with zero exclusions, so it scanned every object file the compiler wrote.
Excluding C:\src, C:\tools, C:\guitest plus the compiler binaries took a
small-file write benchmark from 545 to 983 files/s and reads from 979 to 2257 -
roughly 1.8x and 2.3x, for free. Re-add these if the VM is ever rebuilt.

The boot disk was grown 100 -> 500 GB. On GCE a balanced persistent disk's speed
scales with its provisioned size (140 MB/s + 0.28 per GB), so the old 100 GB disk
was capped at 168 MB/s - it was slow *because* it was small. Aggregate write went
from that 168 ceiling to a measured 262 MB/s. Resize is online: `gcloud compute
disks resize`, then `Resize-Partition` on disk 0 partition 3; C: is the last
partition so nothing blocks the extend, and no reboot is needed.

**Do not benchmark GCE persistent disk with one synchronous writer.** A single
WriteThrough stream is latency-bound and reported only 185 MB/s on the 500 GB
disk, which reads as 'the resize did nothing'. Eight concurrent writers showed the
real 262 MB/s. Use concurrent writers - that is also what a parallel build does.

RDP now prefers the H.264 codec: AVC444ModePreferred=1 (DWORD) under
HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services, effective on the
next connection. That does not touch the real interactivity limit, which is the
~57 ms round-trip from California to us-central1; only moving the VM to a west
coast region fixes that.

The external IP is ephemeral and changes on every stop/start.

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

description: "Seven traps met driving a scratch copy of the built app without screen control (2026-11-04): in-place binary copy gets SIGKILL, Home drops bridge messages while hidden, header popups need a posted NSEvent, lldb std::string args, wx Wrap reuse."
metadata:

  originSessionId: dea8379c-b02c-43a2-a254-4c2259672439
  modified: 2026-11-04T18:59:38.548Z
---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

# Windows GUI test VM (GCP) — working harness

Drives a wxWidgets + OpenGL desktop app on a GPU-less Windows VM in GCP,
headlessly: launch it, screenshot it, click it, verify the result.

Verified 2026-09-07 with OrcaSlicer 2.4.2 portable.

## The VM

    instance : jusprin-win-test
    project  : elegoo-backend
    zone     : us-central1-a
    machine  : n2-standard-8, Windows Server 2022, 100GB pd-balanced
    display  : virtual display device ENABLED (required, see below)
    login    : ssh as guitest with ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine

The external IP is ephemeral and CHANGES on every stop/start. Re-read it with:

    gcloud compute instances describe jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a \
      --project=elegoo-backend \
      --format="value(networkInterfaces[0].accessConfigs[0].natIP)"

then update winssh.sh / winscp.sh.

## Four things that had to be solved

1. **OpenGL.** The app hard-requires OpenGL 3.2 (src/slic3r/GUI/OpenGLManager.cpp)
   and exits below it. Stock Windows software rendering reports 1.1. Fix: drop
   Mesa's `opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` (from pal1000/mesa-dist-win) next
   to the .exe. Reports OpenGL 4.2 on plain CPU.

   Mesa then auto-picks its **d3d12** backend, because the GCE virtual display
   exposes "Microsoft Basic Render Driver" as a D3D12 device — and that path
   crashed on the first frame. run-app.cmd forces the CPU rasterizer with
   `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`.

   Do NOT copy the whole Mesa .7z onto the VM: Windows Defender flags the archive
   as Trojan:Win32/Suschil!rfn and deletes it. Extract the two DLLs elsewhere and
   copy just those — Defender does not object to them, so no AV exclusion is
   needed. (The archive's sha256 matches GitHub's published release digest; the
   detection is a heuristic on the bundle, which also contains Vulkan layers,
   D3D12 compilers and media-foundation encoders we don't use.)

2. **A visible desktop.** A GUI app started from an SSH shell lands in a session
   with no desktop and screenshots come back black. autologon.ps1 creates a local
   admin `guitest` and sets Winlogon AutoAdminLogon so console session 1 is always
   live. Something in the GCE image clears those values after the boot that sets
   them, so startup.ps1 re-applies them on EVERY boot.

3. **Session isolation.** Display APIs, EnumWindows and Get-Process MainWindowTitle
   only see the CALLING session's window station. Run them over SSH and they
   silently report nothing — which reads as "the app has no window" when it does.
   Everything that touches the UI goes through `Invoke-InSession` in harness.ps1,
   which registers a scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive` so it runs in
   session 1, and writes its output to a file to be read back over SSH.

4. **Resolution.** Without a GCE virtual display device the guest falls back to
   Microsoft Basic Display Adapter with no EDID = 640x480, and the app's own
   window is 760x500. Fix (requires the instance to be STOPPED):

       gcloud compute instances stop   jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend
       gcloud compute instances update jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend --enable-display-device
       gcloud compute instances start  jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend

   Then 1920x1080 is available via set-res.ps1.

## Also required by this app

Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime is NOT present on a clean Windows Server image.
Without it the app puts up a modal "WebView2 Runtime" prompt and startup blocks
forever. Installed here as 152.0.4191.66 via the Evergreen bootstrapper:

    Invoke-WebRequest "https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/p/?LinkId=2124703" -OutFile setup.exe
    .\setup.exe /silent /install

This matters more for JusPrin than for stock Orca, since JusPrin's UI is
WebView-based.

content.text:
The Mac test passed. The Windows and Linux tests are still running on their GCP machines, and I'll put all three results together when they finish.

**Mac** (the app copied from the release disk image, run with a separate test data folder so your own JusPrin 2 data was untouched):
- **Install:** macOS accepts the app as signed and notarized by TSD Technology, LLC.
- **Welcome screen:** "Sign up and get 500 free credits", "Use your own AI account" and "Just slice for now" all showed. I chose "Just slice for now".
- **JusPrin 1 import:** the app found your 2 JusPrin 1 printers and imported them, along with 2 filaments and 1 print setting. One print setting ("0.20mm Detail @MK3S 0.6 - Copy") was left behind, and the app's note explains why: it's based on a Prusa preset JusPrin doesn't include. JusPrin 1's folder is only read, never changed.
- **Home:** shows the projects area, the "Set up AI" card with its "Don't show again" link, and the two imported printers.
- **Opening and slicing:** I opened a 20 mm test cube, and it landed on the plate. Slicing finished: about 10 minutes, 3.4 g, $0.07. With no AI set up, the AI panel shows its "No AI connected" state with a Set up AI button.
- **Version:** About JusPrin shows version 2.0.0, built on OrcaSlicer 2.5.0, build 57ae7ef9, which is the release commit.
- **Help guide:** opens and lists all seven pages.
- **Quitting:** the app quit without asking to save or discard, and it left no crash report. This confirms the release notes' claim that JusPrin never asks you to save or discard, which hadn't been checked before.

Two things I saw but didn't look into:
- A macOS system alert flashed during the JusPrin 1 import and was gone before I could read it.
- The app's log says it was "Unable to open the file" for the cube, even though the cube opened fine. My guess is that's an extra file check before the real open, but I haven't confirmed it.

I didn't test signing in or chatting with AI, because that needs your account.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Sourceable helper: `create_dmg <volname> <srcfolder> <output.dmg>` builds a
# compressed DMG, retrying via `retry` (source retry.sh first).
# hdiutil sizes the image from -srcfolder itself and sometimes leaves too
# little room, failing with "No space left on device" on every attempt. An
# explicit -size of the source plus 20% and 50 MB avoids that; the free space
# compresses away in UDZO.
create_dmg() {
  local volname="$1" srcfolder="$2" output="$3"
  local src_mb
  src_mb=$(( $(du -sk "$srcfolder" | cut -f1) / 1024 ))
  retry hdiutil create -volname "$volname" -srcfolder "$srcfolder" \
    -size "$(( src_mb + src_mb / 5 + 50 ))m" -ov -format UDZO "$output"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Turns OrcaSlicer's universal app into JusPrin.app and puts it in a disk image.
#
#   macos_package.sh <OrcaSlicer.app> <version> <output dir>
#
# OrcaSlicer's build names the bundle OrcaSlicer.app with OrcaSlicer's bundle
# identifier, icon and a "JusPrin <build id>" version string. This copies it to
# JusPrin.app and sets JusPrin's identity before anything is signed, because
# editing Info.plist afterwards would break the signature.
#
# Signing: with JUSPRIN_SIGN=1 the app and the disk image are signed with the
# Developer ID certificate in MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID (already in the keychain)
# and notarised with APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT, TEAM_ID and APP_PWD. Otherwise the app
# gets an ad-hoc signature, which keeps the edited bundle consistent but which
# Gatekeeper rejects for a download: that build is for testing only.
set -euo pipefail

source_app="$1"
version="$2"
out_dir="$3"

script_dir="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
repo_root="$(cd -- "${script_dir}/../../../../.." && pwd)"
entitlements="${repo_root}/scripts/disable_validation.entitlements"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${repo_root}/scripts/retry.sh"

work="$(mktemp -d)"
stage="${work}/dmg"
app="${stage}/JusPrin.app"
dmg="${out_dir}/JusPrin_Mac_universal_V${version}.dmg"
mkdir -p "${stage}" "${out_dir}"
cp -R "${source_app}" "${app}"

plist="${app}/Contents/Info.plist"
buddy=/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy
set_key() {
    "${buddy}" -c "Set :$1 $2" "${plist}" 2>/dev/null || "${buddy}" -c "Add :$1 string $2" "${plist}"
}
set_key CFBundleIdentifier io.obico.jusprin
    )
    echo "signing ${#machos[@]} Mach-O files in ${app}"
    sign "${machos[@]}"
    sign --verbose "${app}"
else
    codesign --deep --force --sign - "${app}"
fi
codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 "${app}"

ln -sfn /Applications "${stage}/Applications"
retry hdiutil create -volname "JusPrin" -srcfolder "${stage}" -ov -format UDZO "${dmg}"

if [ "${JUSPRIN_SIGN:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    codesign --force --verbose --timestamp --sign "${MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID}" "${dmg}"
    notary=(--apple-id "${APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT}" --team-id "${TEAM_ID}" --password "${APP_PWD}")
    # notarytool exits 0 when Apple rejects the image, so read the status and
    # print Apple's report, which names each file it rejected.
    result="$(xcrun notarytool submit "${dmg}" "${notary[@]}" --wait --output-format json)"
    echo "${result}"
    if [ "$(plutil -extract status raw - <<<"${result}")" != "Accepted" ]; then
        xcrun notarytool log "$(plutil -extract id raw - <<<"${result}")" "${notary[@]}"
        exit 1
    fi
    retry xcrun stapler staple "${dmg}"
fi

rm -rf "${work}"
echo "${dmg}"

chmod +x "${appdir}/AppRun"

---
name: webkit-click-does-not-focus-buttons
description: "In the app's WKWebView a click never focuses a button, so a menu that closes on blur loses clicks on every row but the focused one; jsdom and Chromium tests hide it. Fixed 2026-10-20 in ActionMenu; repro recipe."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b4c59a23-a9b3-44f2-825e-df7409bab7ee
  modified: 2026-10-20T17:49:56.472Z
---

On macOS WebKit (the app's web view) a mouse press on a `<button>` does not focus it;
it blurs whatever had the focus to `<body>` with `relatedTarget` null. `ActionMenu`
focuses the current row on open and closes on a blur that leaves it, so before
2026-10-20 a click on any OTHER row closed the menu on mouse-down and the click
never arrived. Kenneth hit it as "clicking an Anthropic model to switch from an
OpenAI model does nothing"; it also broke other thinking levels, + menu items after
the first, and Delete in the chat's ⋯ menu (the blur rule dates from 8334b3395b,
2026-09-23). Fix (claude/composer-redesign, uncommitted at the time):
`onMouseDown={e => e.preventDefault()}` on `.chat-menu-list`, guarded by
ActionMenu.test.tsx ("keeps the focus where it is when a row is pressed").

**Why:** vitest (jsdom), userEvent and Playwright/Chromium all focus a clicked
button, so every test passed while the app was broken. The host test for the same
switch passed too.

**How to apply:** for any web control that closes on blur or depends on focus after
a click, test the press in real WebKit. Recipe: a ~60-line Swift program with an
NSWindow + WKWebView, focus element A from script, then `NSApp.sendEvent` a
leftMouseDown/Up NSEvent at element B and read a log back with
`evaluateJavaScript` (`swiftc -O repro.swift -o repro && ./repro`, no permissions
needed). The live app was unreachable that day: its window was on a Space
`app_bring_to_current_space` refused to move. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[composer-model-pickers]].

input.ask: Fix the Linux certificate question and blank video, then rebuild the draft?

content.text:
2.0.0 installs and works on all three systems: opening a model and slicing it work on each. Windows and the Mac had no problems that would block the release. Linux has one that would: a certificate question appears every time the app starts.

**Linux** (the AppImage, on the Ubuntu 24.04 test machine):
- **Certificate question on every start.** Before the app opens, a dialog titled "OrcaSlicer" says "use system SSL certificate: /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt … Do you want to continue?". Answering No closes the app without a word, and "Remember my choice" is unticked by default.
  - The cause: the security library bundled in the app looks for certificates in a folder on the build machine.
  - JusPrin inherited this from OrcaSlicer, whose AppImage has shown the same dialog since at least 2024 ([OrcaSlicer issue #5333](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/issues/5333)).
- **Blank welcome video.** The video uses H.264, which stock Ubuntu can't play without extra codecs.
- **Dropdown clicks.** In a dropdown with a search box, clicking a brand or model closed the list without choosing it, while typing and pressing Enter worked. The tester saw this only with simulated clicks, and that list already contains the earlier fix for this kind of WebKit focus problem. I can't count it as a bug until someone sees it with a real mouse.
- **Installing from the file manager.** Once "Allow this file to run as a program" is ticked, double-clicking starts the app. It doesn't need the `libfuse2` library. It adds no menu entry, and the file shows a generic icon.
- Everything else passed: Home, slicing (about 19 min, 3.7 g), About (2.0.0, build 57ae7ef9), the guide, the AI panel and quitting.

**Windows** (the installer and the portable zip): every step passed.
- The installer puts JusPrin in `C:\Program Files\JusPrin` and adds a Start menu entry. Settings › Apps lists JusPrin 2.0.0 by Obico, and uninstalling cleanly keeps your projects.
- SmartScreen warns about an unknown publisher, as expected for an unsigned build.
- Small things to tidy later:
  - The last installer page has no "Launch JusPrin" checkbox.
  - Reinstalling 2.0.0 over 2.0.0 calls the installed copy "the old version".
  - The installer's side picture is the generic one.
  - Two leftover build folders get installed: `include\stb_dxt` and `lib\cmake`.

**Mac:** everything passed, as I reported earlier. The blank Applications box you saw in the disk image window comes from Finder on this Mac, not from how JusPrin builds the image.
- I made 8 fresh test images, each containing only that same kind of link to /Applications. Finder drew the icon in some and a blank box in others, whichever file system the image used.
- Bambu Studio's and Claude's images use the same link.
- One other macOS 26 user reported the same blank icon, and the disk-image tool's developer concluded it was a problem with that one Mac ([C-Command forum](https://forum.c-command.com/t/application-folder-icon-not-visible-in-dmg-on-macos-26/17498)).

So I'm not changing anything for the blank icon.

My proposed fixes for the two Linux problems:
- **Certificate question:** the AppImage's launch script points the app at the distribution's own certificate file before the app starts. That change lives only in JusPrin's packaging script, `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/appimage.sh`.
- **Welcome video:** add a WebM copy of the video, which Ubuntu plays out of the box, and keep the H.264 copy for the other systems.

Either fix means fast-forwarding `main` again and re-running the release workflow, which replaces the draft's files. That takes about two hours, and then the Linux test runs again.

You're running JusPrin 2.0.0 from Applications right now, so I closed my test copy. Both share an app id, and my clicks could have landed in your window. Both VMs are stopped.

Fix and rebuild

"""Run the Linux package hooks with host binaries in an AppDir fixture.

This verifies launcher dispatch, arguments and MCP pipes without a GUI. It is
not a Linux ELF dependency audit or proof of an actual mounted AppImage.
"""
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import shlex
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

from test_bridge_process import BRIDGE, Child, Peer, ROOT, request


@unittest.skipUnless(os.name == "posix" and BRIDGE.is_file(), "Requires POSIX and a built MCP helper")
class LinuxPackageTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="jusprin-package-")
        self.addCleanup(temporary.cleanup)
        self.root = Path(temporary.name).resolve()
        self.package = self.root / "Kenny's 打印 AppDir"
        self.build = self.root / "build output"
        self.build.mkdir()
        for directory in ("bin", "libexec", "lib/orca-runtime"):
            (self.package / directory).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.main = self.build / "orca-slicer"
        self.main.write_text("fixture")
        shutil.copy2(BRIDGE, self.build / "jusprin-mcp")
        self.source = (ROOT / "src/dev-utils/platform/unix/build_linux_image.sh.in").read_text()
        hook = re.search(r'    if \[ -n "@SLIC3R_PACKAGE_EXTRA_SCRIPT@" \]; then\n.*?\n    fi',
                         self.source, re.DOTALL)
        self.assertIsNotNone(hook, "Packaging must invoke the extra-binary hook")
        self.hook = hook.group().replace("@SLIC3R_PACKAGE_EXTRA_SCRIPT@", str(
            ROOT / "src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Mcp/Bridge/package_linux.sh"))
        self.environment = dict(os.environ, ORIGINAL_BINARY_LOCATION=str(self.main), APPDIR=str(self.package))
        self.run_package_hook(check=True)

        # Generate exactly the launcher heredoc used by the upstream packager,
        # then perform the same rename that build_appimage.sh makes.
        begin = self.source.index("cat << EOF >@SLIC3R_APP_CMD@")
        end = self.source.index("\nEOF", begin) + len("\nEOF")
        generate = self.source[begin:end].replace("@SLIC3R_APP_CMD@", "orca-slicer")
        subprocess.run(["bash"], input=generate, text=True, cwd=self.package, check=True)
        self.launcher = self.package / "AppRun"
        (self.package / "orca-slicer").rename(self.launcher)
        self.launcher.chmod(0o755)
        self.discovery = self.root / "Kenny's data; $literal 打印.json"

    def run_package_hook(self, check=False):
        return subprocess.run(["bash", "-e", "-c", self.hook], env=self.environment,
                              capture_output=True, text=True, check=check)

    def child(self):
        child = Child(self.discovery, env={"APPDIR": str(self.package)},
                      command=[str(self.launcher), "--mcp-bridge"])
        self.addCleanup(lambda: self.assertEqual(child.stop()[0], 0))
        return child

    def test_packaged_helper_handshake_and_offline_without_gui_runtime(self):

        # not invoke graphics or WebKit checks on this route.
        child = self.child()

# Sourced by the package launcher before locale, graphics, or WebKit setup.
# Leave ordinary GUI launches and their arguments entirely to Orca's launcher.
if [ "${1:-}" = "--mcp-bridge" ]; then
    shift
    # The helper needs only its packaged C++/Boost runtime, not GUI libraries.
    export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$DIR/lib/orca-runtime:$DIR/bin${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH}"
    exec "$DIR/bin/jusprin-mcp" "$@"
fi

# The bundled OpenSSL looks for certificates under the build machine's prefix.
# When it finds none, OrcaSlicer's startup (CurlGlobalInit) picks the distro's
# CA bundle itself but first asks "use system SSL certificate ... Do you want
# to continue?" on every launch. Name the bundle here, from the same list in
# the same order, so the app finds it and never asks. A bundle the user set is
# left alone.
if [ -z "${SSL_CERT_FILE:-}" ]; then
    for bundle in /etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt \
        /usr/share/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt /usr/local/share/certs/ca-root-nss.crt \
        /etc/ssl/cert.pem /etc/ssl/ca-bundle.pem; do
        if [ -f "$bundle" ]; then
            export SSL_CERT_FILE="$bundle"
            break
        fi
    done
fi
EOF

# JusPrin Linux GUI test VM

A GCP VM for building JusPrin on Linux and testing its GUI, either by hand over
remote desktop or by script on a headless display.

| | |
|---|---|
| Instance | `jusprin-linux-test`, project `elegoo-backend`, zone `us-west2-a` (Los Angeles, for low latency from California) |
| Machine | n2-standard-16 (16 vCPU, 64 GB), 300 GB pd-balanced, no GPU |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, XFCE desktop |
| Toolchain | Ubuntu's gcc 13, CMake 4.3.0 (same as the CI runner, in /opt), Node 24.11.1 (in /opt) |
| Checkout | `~/JusPrin` on branch `jusprin-dev` (user `kenneth`) |
| OpenGL | Mesa llvmpipe, OpenGL 4.5 core, software rendering |

The VM has no service account, so it cannot call GCP APIs. It cannot fetch the
private GitHub repo either; send commits with a git bundle (below).

## Scripts (run on the Mac)

- `./vmssh.sh '<command>'` runs a command on the VM.
- `./vmscp.sh <src> <dst>` copies files; write `VM:~/path` for the VM side.
- `./connect-rdp.sh` starts the VM if stopped, prints the login, and holds an SSH
  tunnel open. Point Windows App (Microsoft Remote Desktop) at `localhost:33890`,
  user `kenneth`. xrdp listens only on the VM's own localhost, so the project-wide
  `default-allow-rdp` firewall rule does not expose it.
- `env.sh` holds the instance name and forces the `ai-agent` service account. It
  also points gcloud at uv's standalone Python 3.12, because Homebrew's Python lost
  its OpenSSL library when Homebrew moved from openssl@3 to openssl@4.

## Scripts (copied to the VM's home folder)

- `~/vm-run-app.sh [args]` starts the built app on headless display `:99` (Xvfb
  with the xfwm4 window manager) with data dir `~/jusprin-test-data`. Log:
  `~/app.log`. It sets `SSL_CERT_FILE`; without it OrcaSlicer's Linux build stops
  at startup on a dialog asking which certificate file to use.
- `~/vm-screenshot.sh` saves display `:99` to `~/shot.png`.
- Click with `DISPLAY=:99 xdotool mousemove X Y click 1`. Screenshot pixels equal
  screen coordinates (1920x1080).
- Stop the app with `pkill -x orca-slicer`. Never `pkill -f orca-slicer` over
  ssh: it matches the ssh command's own text and kills the session.

## Build

```bash
# First time on a fresh VM: deps (about 25 min) then app and tests (about 30 min)
cd ~/JusPrin && ./build_linux.sh -dst -j 16
# After code changes: app and tests only
cd ~/JusPrin && ./build_linux.sh -st -j 16
```

The app lands in `~/JusPrin/build/package/bin/orca-slicer`. Run long builds
detached so an ssh disconnect does not kill them:

```bash
setsid nohup bash -c 'set -o pipefail; ./build_linux.sh -st -j 16 2>&1 | tee ~/build.log; echo BUILD_EXIT=$? >> ~/build.log' >/dev/null 2>&1 </dev/null &
```

Tests: `cd ~/JusPrin/build && DISPLAY=:99 ctest -C Release -j 8`.

## Sending new commits

```bash
git bundle create f.bundle jusprin-dev ^<commit the VM already has>
./vmscp.sh f.bundle VM:~/
./vmssh.sh 'cd ~/JusPrin && git pull ~/f.bundle jusprin-dev'
```

## Cost

The VM bills while running. Stop it when idle:

```bash
gcloud compute instances stop jusprin-linux-test --project elegoo-backend --zone us-west2-a
```

The external IP is ephemeral and changes on each start; the scripts look it up
by name, so nothing needs editing.
#!/bin/bash
# Run a command on the VM: ./vmssh.sh 'uptime'
. "$(dirname "$0")/env.sh"
exec gcloud compute ssh "$VM" --project "$PROJECT" --zone "$ZONE" --command "$*"
#!/bin/bash
# Copy files: ./vmscp.sh local.txt VM:~/  or  ./vmscp.sh VM:~/shot.png .
. "$(dirname "$0")/env.sh"
args=(); for a in "$@"; do args+=("${a/#VM:/$VM:}"); done
exec gcloud compute scp "${args[@]}" --project "$PROJECT" --zone "$ZONE"

He asked for ideas.

content.text:
I can't fix it from inside JusPrin's disk image, because the cause isn't in the image. On this Mac, Finder draws a blank Applications box for other companies' disk images too, including Claude's and Bambu Studio's.

**What I tested**
- **Same moment, same Mac:** I opened Claude's, Bambu Studio's and JusPrin's disk images together. Claude's and Bambu Studio's drew the blue Applications folder and JusPrin's was blank, so at first it looked like our problem.
- **Ruled out:** neither the file system (APFS or HFS+), nor the window layout file, nor the signature, nor JusPrin's icon files explains it. Test images with each change came out blank or fine with no pattern.
- **The pattern:** I opened four Bambu Studio and three JusPrin images in a row. All four Bambu ones drew the folder, and so did two of the three JusPrin ones. The JusPrin window that came up blank was the one opened last. In your screenshot, too, you're looking at the window you just opened.
- **The deciding test:** I then opened a Bambu Studio image and Claude's image last. Both showed the same blank dashed box in place of the Applications folder.

The Applications entry is a link to the `/Applications` folder, and Bambu Studio's and Claude's images use the same kind of link. Finder on macOS 26.3 sometimes fails to draw its icon in the window that just opened. Dragging the app onto the blank box still installs it. One other person reported the same thing for a different disk image tool on macOS 26. That tool's developer opened the same file on macOS 26 and saw the icon, and put it down to that person's Mac's icon cache ([C-Command forum thread](https://forum.c-command.com/t/application-folder-icon-not-visible-in-dmg-on-macos-26/17498)). Restarting Finder or the Mac may clear it here, but I haven't tried that because it would close your Finder windows.

**Decision needed:** should the disk image stay as it is, or should I try a workaround? The workaround would replace the link with a Finder shortcut that carries its own copy of the folder icon, so Finder wouldn't have to look the icon up. It costs about an hour, it's not how Claude, Bambu Studio and PrusaSlicer ship, and since the bug is random I can't confirm it helps on other Macs. I'd leave it as it is, because those three apps ship the same link and the box still works when someone drags onto it. Do you want it left as it is?

**The Linux fixes:** the GitHub release build with both Linux fixes, the certificate question and the welcome clip, is still running. When it finishes I'll retest the new Linux AppImage and Mac disk image.
Leave it

# Windows GUI test VM (GCP) — working harness

Drives a wxWidgets + OpenGL desktop app on a GPU-less Windows VM in GCP,
headlessly: launch it, screenshot it, click it, verify the result.

Verified 2026-09-07 with OrcaSlicer 2.4.2 portable.

## The VM

    instance : jusprin-win-test
    project  : elegoo-backend
    zone     : us-central1-a
    machine  : n2-standard-8, Windows Server 2022, 100GB pd-balanced
    display  : virtual display device ENABLED (required, see below)
    login    : ssh as guitest with ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine

The external IP is ephemeral and CHANGES on every stop/start. Re-read it with:

    gcloud compute instances describe jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a \
      --project=elegoo-backend \
      --format="value(networkInterfaces[0].accessConfigs[0].natIP)"

then update winssh.sh / winscp.sh.

## Four things that had to be solved

1. **OpenGL.** The app hard-requires OpenGL 3.2 (src/slic3r/GUI/OpenGLManager.cpp)
   and exits below it. Stock Windows software rendering reports 1.1. Fix: drop
   Mesa's `opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` (from pal1000/mesa-dist-win) next
   to the .exe. Reports OpenGL 4.2 on plain CPU.

   Mesa then auto-picks its **d3d12** backend, because the GCE virtual display
   exposes "Microsoft Basic Render Driver" as a D3D12 device — and that path
   crashed on the first frame. run-app.cmd forces the CPU rasterizer with
   `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`.

   Do NOT copy the whole Mesa .7z onto the VM: Windows Defender flags the archive
   as Trojan:Win32/Suschil!rfn and deletes it. Extract the two DLLs elsewhere and
   copy just those — Defender does not object to them, so no AV exclusion is
   needed. (The archive's sha256 matches GitHub's published release digest; the
   detection is a heuristic on the bundle, which also contains Vulkan layers,
   D3D12 compilers and media-foundation encoders we don't use.)

2. **A visible desktop.** A GUI app started from an SSH shell lands in a session
   with no desktop and screenshots come back black. autologon.ps1 creates a local
   admin `guitest` and sets Winlogon AutoAdminLogon so console session 1 is always
   live. Something in the GCE image clears those values after the boot that sets
   them, so startup.ps1 re-applies them on EVERY boot.

3. **Session isolation.** Display APIs, EnumWindows and Get-Process MainWindowTitle
   only see the CALLING session's window station. Run them over SSH and they
   silently report nothing — which reads as "the app has no window" when it does.
   Everything that touches the UI goes through `Invoke-InSession` in harness.ps1,
   which registers a scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive` so it runs in
   session 1, and writes its output to a file to be read back over SSH.

4. **Resolution.** Without a GCE virtual display device the guest falls back to
   Microsoft Basic Display Adapter with no EDID = 640x480, and the app's own
   window is 760x500. Fix (requires the instance to be STOPPED):

## Also required by this app

Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime is NOT present on a clean Windows Server image.
Without it the app puts up a modal "WebView2 Runtime" prompt and startup blocks
forever. Installed here as 152.0.4191.66 via the Evergreen bootstrapper:

    Invoke-WebRequest "https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/p/?LinkId=2124703" -OutFile setup.exe
    .\setup.exe /silent /install

This matters more for JusPrin than for stock Orca, since JusPrin's UI is
WebView-based.

## Files

    startup.ps1      GCE windows-startup-script-ps1: OpenSSH, port 22 firewall,
                     authorized_keys, calls autologon.ps1. Runs every boot.
    autologon.ps1    Creates guitest + sets AutoAdminLogon. Idempotent.
    harness.ps1      Invoke-InSession / Take-Screenshot. Source this first.

    probe.ps1        Lists session 1's real windows to C:\guitest\windows.txt.
    focus-app.ps1    Closes leftover task consoles, maximizes the app window.
    click.ps1        Clicks the "x,y" in C:\guitest\click.txt.
    set-res.ps1      Sets 1920x1080. Must run in-session.
    install-app.ps1  Downloads the app, places the Mesa DLLs beside the .exe.
    run-app.cmd      Launches the app with llvmpipe forced, detached.

# Helper functions for driving a GUI app in the auto-logon console session.
# A process started from an SSH session has no desktop; a scheduled task with
# LogonType Interactive lands in guitest's live session 1 instead.

function Invoke-InSession {
    param([string]$TaskName, [string]$Exe, [string]$ArgLine = "", [string]$WorkDir = "C:\guitest")
    $a = if ($ArgLine) {
        New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute $Exe -Argument $ArgLine -WorkingDirectory $WorkDir
    } else {
        New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute $Exe -WorkingDirectory $WorkDir
    }
    $p = New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal -UserId "guitest" -LogonType Interactive -RunLevel Highest
    $s = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -AllowStartIfOnBatteries -DontStopIfGoingOnBatteries `
             -ExecutionTimeLimit ([TimeSpan]::Zero)
    Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName $TaskName -Action $a -Principal $p -Settings $s -Force | Out-Null
    Start-ScheduledTask -TaskName $TaskName
}

function Take-Screenshot {
    Invoke-InSession -TaskName "GuiShot" `
        -Exe "C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe" `
        -ArgLine "-NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File C:\guitest\screenshot.ps1"
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 4
}

content.text:
I installed the rebuilt 2.0.0 on the Windows and Linux test machines and took a picture of every step. Both install correctly and JusPrin opens afterwards. I've sent you the two picture sheets, with a caption on each step. They're also saved in `.claude/release-2.0.0-shots/` in the JusPrin checkout.

**Linux** (Ubuntu 24.04 with the Xfce desktop and its Thunar file manager):
- The first double-click on the downloaded AppImage opens the file manager's "choose an app" dialog. Every AppImage does this until it's marked runnable.
- After ticking "Allow this file to run as a program" in Properties, a double-click opens JusPrin's welcome screen.
- The certificate question no longer appears, and the welcome clip plays. Both Linux fixes are confirmed in the rebuilt file.

**Windows** (Windows Server 2022):
- **Windows warnings:** opening the installer brings up the "Windows protected your PC" warning (Publisher: Unknown publisher, then "Run anyway"), and then the yellow "unknown publisher" admin prompt. Both come from the installer not being code-signed, which we already knew.
- **Installer pages:** welcome, license (AGPL v3), install location `C:\Program Files\JusPrin` (622 MB), Start-menu folder, progress, and finish. The Start-menu entry has the JusPrin icon and opens the app.
- **Things that look unfinished:**
  - The welcome and finish pages use NSIS's generic computer picture, not JusPrin artwork. NSIS is the program that builds the Windows installer.
  - Every page's footer reads "Nullsoft Install System v3.13".
  - The progress line names files such as "Extract: OrcaSlicer.dll".
  - The finish page has no "Launch JusPrin" checkbox.
  - Two folders only developers need, `include` and `lib\cmake`, get installed with the app.

**Mac:** GitHub cancelled the Mac build twice because no hosted Mac machine was free. Its status page says Actions is working normally, and this repository's nightly build is hitting the same thing. I've set the release build to retry up to six times. Once it succeeds, I'll test the new Mac disk image. Both test VMs are stopped.

**Decision needed:** should I polish the Windows installer before 2.0.0 ships? The footer text, the missing launch checkbox, the two developer folders and the side picture can all be set in JusPrin's own packaging file (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/packaging.cmake`), without touching OrcaSlicer's code. The side picture needs a 164×314 JusPrin image, which I'd make from the brand assets in `resources/jusprin/`. The "OrcaSlicer.dll" file name would stay, because renaming it is a large change in OrcaSlicer's own code.
- **Polish now:** about an hour of work, plus one more full release build (about two hours, longer while GitHub's Macs are scarce). The run already underway would be thrown away.
- **Ship as is:** the installer works and Windows users get JusPrin, but it looks generic, and the polish moves to 2.0.1.

I'd polish it now. The Mac build is stuck waiting anyway, so the extra build costs less time than it normally would, and the installer is the first thing a Windows user sees.

input.prompt: What is the problem, which macOS runner labels are affected, any GitHub staff responses, dates, and which workarounds worked (which labels got runners)?

result.output:
**Problem:** Standard `macos-latest` ARM64 jobs stayed queued for about 15 minutes, then were cancelled before any step ran. Job metadata showed `runner_id: 0` and an empty steps array. The workflow concluded as failure and the job as cancelled. Annotations said "The job was not acquired by Runner of type hosted even after multiple attempts" and "Due to capacity constraints, jobs targeting macOS arm64 runners may experience longer queue times." Some users also saw an "Internal server error."

**Affected labels:** `macos-latest` (ARM64). The original poster said other jobs got a `macos-26-arm64` runner between failures, so allocation was intermittent. One user reported that `macos-latest` maps to the macos-26 arm64 image.

**GitHub staff responses:** None. The only reply from GitHub is an automated bot message acknowledging product feedback. The discussion is marked unanswered. The original poster said the public status page reported all systems operational, and another user said githubstatus.com showed no Actions incidents.

**Dates reported:**
- **Nov 2:** Failures around 16:21–16:36, 18:00–18:15 and 19:00–19:15 UTC.
- **Nov 3:** Multiple users reported the same issue, including on public repositories.
- **Nov 4:** A user said the problem had persisted since at least the previous day and came and went. Another reported failures in the evening (CET) but success in the morning.
- **Nov 5:** Users reported it had lasted "about 3 days" or "a few days," and one confirmed it across five consecutive runs.
- **Nov 6:** More users reported the same issue.
- **Nov 9:** A user said manually re-running failed workflows helps for small CI but doesn't scale.

**Workarounds:**
- **Pinning to `macos-15`** worked for one user. The job got a runner immediately, while `macos-latest` failed three times in a row.
- **Running on a personal MacBook** as a self-hosted runner worked for one user.
- **Scheduling jobs for mornings** helped one user, though this is a timing workaround rather than a fix.
- **Re-running the workflow** did not work for at least one user, and others said manual re-runs were unreliable.

input.ask: Polish the Windows installer before 2.0.0?

content.text:
The Mac part of the 2.0.0 release build still hasn't run. GitHub cancelled it six more times between 17:11 and 18:49 UTC because it had no free Mac machine to give it. The Windows and Linux files from the same run are already built.

**Why it keeps failing:** each Mac job waits 15 minutes for a GitHub-hosted Mac, gets none, and is cancelled without running a single step.
- This repository's nightly build hit the same wall at 17:39 UTC.
- GitHub's status page shows Actions as working normally.
- Other projects have reported the same thing since about 2 November ([community discussion](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/211885), [one project's issue](https://github.com/fivvi-app/fivvi/issues/413)). GitHub hasn't answered any of these reports.
- One project said pinning to `macos-15` got it a runner when `macos-latest` didn't. We already use `macos-15`, so that workaround doesn't apply to us.

**What I'm doing about it:** Mac machines did take this repository's builds at 00:38 and 04:25 UTC today. That fits the reports that it works at quieter hours. So I started a new loop that re-runs only the cancelled Mac jobs, up to 48 times, which covers the night.
- If a Mac job ever starts and then fails for a real reason, the loop stops instead of retrying.
- Once the Mac jobs succeed, the run combines the two Mac builds into one disk image and uploads it to the draft release. Then I'll download it and test it on your Mac.

I didn't switch to a different Mac machine type. The cached build dependencies are stored per machine type, so a switch would rebuild them from scratch, which takes hours. It would also mean changing the build workflow on `main` again.
Polish it now

# release archive from SourceForge instead of going through the Chocolatey
      # community feed, which hosted runners often cannot reach. Prepending it to
      # PATH also makes cpack use it over the NSIS preinstalled on some images.
      - name: Restore NSIS
        id: nsis-cache
        if: runner.os == 'Windows' && !vars.SELF_HOSTED
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v6
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/nsis
          key: nsis-${{ env.NSIS_VERSION }}

      - name: Install NSIS
        if: runner.os == 'Windows' && !vars.SELF_HOSTED
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          dir "C:/Program Files (x86)/Windows Kits/10/Include"
          $nsisDir = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'nsis'
          $makensis = Join-Path $nsisDir 'makensis.exe'
          if (-not (Test-Path $makensis)) {
            $zip = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP "nsis-$env:NSIS_VERSION.zip"
            curl.exe -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 15 -o $zip "https://downloads.sourceforge.net/project/nsis/NSIS%203/$env:NSIS_VERSION/nsis-$env:NSIS_VERSION.zip"
            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "NSIS $env:NSIS_VERSION download failed." }
            if ((Get-FileHash $zip -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -ne $env:NSIS_SHA256) {
              throw "NSIS $env:NSIS_VERSION archive does not match its pinned SHA256."
            }
            Expand-Archive $zip $env:RUNNER_TEMP
            Move-Item (Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP "nsis-$env:NSIS_VERSION") $nsisDir
          }
          & $makensis /VERSION
          $nsisDir | Out-File -Append -FilePath $env:GITHUB_PATH -Encoding utf8

      - name: Save NSIS
        if: runner.os == 'Windows' && !vars.SELF_HOSTED && steps.nsis-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@v6
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/nsis
          key: nsis-${{ env.NSIS_VERSION }}

      # Windows release builds are Authenticode-signed with the company's key in Google Cloud KMS
      # (README, Code Signing Policy): pushes, schedules and manual runs of main and release/* in
      # this repository, once the WINDOWS_SIGN_* variables are set. The Workload Identity provider
      # accepts tokens from nothing else. This runs before the build so that CMake wires signing
      # into the NSIS installer.
      - name: Configure code signing
        id: codesign
        if: runner.os == 'Windows' && github.repository == 'OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer' && (github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/heads/release/')) && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && vars.WINDOWS_SIGN_KMS_KEY != ''
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          CERT_CHAIN: ${{ vars.WINDOWS_SIGN_CERT_CHAIN }}
          KMS_KEY: ${{ vars.WINDOWS_SIGN_KMS_KEY }}
        run: |
          $jar = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP "jsign-$env:JSIGN_VERSION.jar"
          curl.exe -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 15 -o $jar "https://github.com/ebourg/jsign/releases/download/$env:JSIGN_VERSION/jsign-$env:JSIGN_VERSION.jar"
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Jsign $env:JSIGN_VERSION download failed." }
          if ((Get-FileHash $jar -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -ne $env:JSIGN_SHA256) {
            throw "Jsign $env:JSIGN_VERSION does not match its pinned SHA256."
          }
          $cert = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'codesign-chain.pem'
          Set-Content -LiteralPath $cert -Value $env:CERT_CHAIN
          "ORCA_SIGN_JSIGN=$jar"           | Out-File -Append -FilePath $env:GITHUB_ENV -Encoding utf8
          "ORCA_SIGN_CERTFILE=$cert"       | Out-File -Append -FilePath $env:GITHUB_ENV -Encoding utf8
          "ORCA_SIGN_KMS_KEY=$env:KMS_KEY" | Out-File -Append -FilePath $env:GITHUB_ENV -Encoding utf8

      - name: Set up Java for code signing
        if: steps.codesign.outcome == 'success'
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6

No, OrcaSlicer users don't see these warnings anymore, and yes, signing JusPrin's installer fixes at least one of the two. OrcaSlicer added Windows signing on 2026-11-06 (upstream commit 73e64d3bc5, "Sign Windows release and nightly builds in CI"). I read the signature on the 2.5.0 installer: it's signed by **ORCASLICER PTE. LTD.**, with a Sectigo code-signing certificate.

**JusPrin already has OrcaSlicer's signing code, but it never runs.** It came in with the 2.5.0 merge, as `scripts/sign_windows.ps1` and the "Configure code signing" and "Sign Windows binaries" steps in `.github/workflows/build_orca.yml`. Those steps only run when all of these hold:
- the repository is `OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer`;
- the branch is `main` or `release/*`;
- the `WINDOWS_SIGN_*` repository settings exist.

Their private key sits in Google Cloud KMS, which signs the files without the key ever leaving it. A GitHub workflow can reach it only from their repository.

**What signing would do for us:**
- **The yellow admin prompt goes away.** It turns into the normal blue prompt with "Verified publisher" and our company name. That happens as soon as the files are signed.
- **The blue "Windows protected your PC" screen may not go away right away.** That screen is SmartScreen, Windows' download reputation check. I'm going from memory here, not something I checked today: a brand-new certificate starts with no reputation, so the warning can keep showing until enough people have installed files signed with it. I also recall that since 2024 Microsoft no longer gives the pricier "EV" certificates an instant pass. Either way, signing is what lets the reputation build up. Unsigned files never earn it.

**What it would take:**
- **A certificate in the company's name.** You'd buy it from a certificate seller such as Sectigo, or use Microsoft's own signing service (Azure Trusted Signing), which has rules on who can sign up. The seller checks the company's identity, which usually takes days to a couple of weeks. This part is yours to do. I can't do it.
- **Keeping the key in Google Cloud KMS, as OrcaSlicer does.** Since 2023, sellers have had to issue code-signing keys on hardware, and KMS counts. We already use Google Cloud, so I could set up the key ring and the permission that lets our release workflow use it.
- **A small change to JusPrin's workflow** so the signing steps run in this repository, set to our release run instead of `OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer`. That's a few lines in an OrcaSlicer-owned workflow file. The signing script itself can be reused as is.

**Decision needed:** should 2.0.0 wait for a signed Windows installer? If it waits, the release slips by however long the certificate checks take, likely one to two weeks, plus the certificate cost: roughly a few hundred dollars a year, or a monthly fee for Microsoft's service. If it doesn't wait, 2.0.0 ships unsigned with both warnings, and signing arrives in 2.0.x once the certificate comes. My pick is to ship 2.0.0 unsigned and start buying the certificate now, so the signing change lands as soon as it's ready. Do you want to wait for signing, or ship unsigned?
